module1.stem: Point O is the center of a circle, and points B and C lie on the circle. The measure of angle BOC is 121°. What is the measure, in degrees, of major arc BC?

module1.stem: The graph of a system of an absolute value function and a linear function is shown. What is the solution (x, y) to this system of two equations?
module1.rationale: The drawn curve is y = |x − 2| + 6 and the drawn line is y = 2x + 8; they meet at (0, 8).
reasons: named the lowest point of the curve rather than where the line crosses it
wrote the two coordinates the wrong way round
named the origin rather than the point the two graphs share

module1.stem:
r = yh
The given equation relates the numbers r, y, and h. Which equation correctly expresses y in terms of r and h?
module1.rationale: Multiplying both sides of r = yh by whatever divides y and dividing by whatever multiplies it gives y = r/h.
reasons: turned the fraction upside down
multiplied every letter together instead of dividing
added the letters instead of multiplying them

module1.stem: For a 5-week period in a town in Oregon, the lowest recorded temperature was 39 degrees Fahrenheit (°F) and the highest recorded temperature was 53°F. Which inequality is true for any recorded temperature t, in °F, in this town for this 5-week period?
module1.rationale: Every recorded value is at least the smallest, 39, and at most the largest, 53; both were recorded, so both ends belong to the range and 39 ≤ t ≤ 53.
reasons: kept only the smallest recorded value and read it as a cap rather than as the bottom of the range
kept only the largest recorded value and read it as a floor rather than as the top of the range
used the largest recorded value as the bottom of the range and the sum of the two as the top

module1.stem: On a 135-mile trip, Cameron drove at an average speed of 55 miles per hour for the first x hours. He then completed the trip, driving at an average speed of 40 miles per hour for the remaining y hours. If x = 1, what is the value of y ?
module1.rationale: 1 hours at 55 miles per hour covers 55 miles, so 80 miles of the 135 are left to drive at 40 miles per hour.

module1.stem: A circle has a circumference of 37π meters. What is the diameter, in meters, of the circle?
module1.rationale: From circumference = 37π, the radius is 37/2, so the diameter is 37.

module1.stem:
H = 150p + 65
The formula above shows the relationship between Renata's target heart rate H, in beats per minute (bpm), and the intensity level p of different activities. When p = 0, Renata has a resting heart rate. When p = 1, Renata has a maximum heart rate. It is recommended that p be between 0.3 and 0.4 for Renata when training. Which of the following inequalities describes Renata's target training heart rate?
module1.rationale: The smallest the quantity can be is 65 + 150(0.3) = 110, and the largest is 65 + 150(0.4) = 125; the multiplier is positive, so the ends keep their order and 110 ≤ H ≤ 125.
reasons: added the resting heart rate at the top of the range but not at the bottom
left the resting heart rate out of both ends of the range
added the resting heart rate at the bottom of the range but not at the top

module1.stem: Which of the following is equivalent to ¹⁰√(z² + 6z + 9), where z > 0?
module1.rationale: z² + 6z + 9 is (z + 3)², and a root of index 10 divides that exponent by 10.
reasons: wrote the exponent as 1 over the index and forgot the 2 the square contributes
used the root's index as the exponent instead of dividing by it
factored the trinomial but never took the root

module1.stem: A shipping service restricts the dimensions of the boxes it will ship for a certain type of service. The restriction states that for boxes shaped like rectangular prisms, the sum of the perimeter of the base of the box and the height of the box cannot exceed 135 inches. The perimeter of the base is determined using the width and length of the box. If a box has a height of 35 inches and its length is 1.5 times the width, which inequality shows the allowable width x, in inches, of the box?
module1.rationale: The base has perimeter 2(x + 1.5x) = 5x, so 5x + 35 ≤ 135, leaving x ≤ 20; a width is positive, so 0 < x ≤ 20.
reasons: left the height out of the cap altogether
added the width and the length once each instead of finding the whole perimeter
used four widths, as though the base were a square

module1.stem: Point X lies on a circle of radius 12 in the xy-plane and has coordinates (0, −12). Point O is the center of the circle and has coordinates (0, 0). Point Y also lies on the circle and has coordinates (x, 12), where x is a constant. Which of the following could be the positive measure of angle XOY, in radians?
module1.rationale: Y must be (0, 12), the far end of the diameter through X, so angle XOY is a half turn plus any whole number of full turns: π + 30π = 31π.
reasons: a half-integer multiple of π stops a quarter turn away, at (12, 0)
an even multiple of π is a whole number of full turns, which ends back at X
a half-integer multiple of π stops a quarter turn away, at (−12, 0)

module1.stem: The mean score of 19 players in a basketball game was 51.5 points. If the highest individual score is removed, the mean score of the remaining 18 players becomes 47.5 points. What was the highest score?
module1.rationale: The 19 values total 978.5 and the 18 that remain total 855, a difference of 123.5.
reasons: reported how far the mean fell, not the value that was taken away
swapped the two counts, using one fewer for the original group
subtracted 19 times the new mean instead of 18 times

module1.stem: A team hosting an event to raise money for new uniforms plans to sell at least 90 tickets before this event and at least 340 tickets during this event to raise a total of at least $3,460 from all tickets sold. The price of a ticket during this event is $5 less than the price of a ticket before this event. Which inequality represents this situation, where x is the price, in dollars, of a ticket sold during this event?
module1.rationale: A ticket before the event costs 5 dollars more than one during it, so it costs x + 5 dollars, and the two groups together raise 90(x + 5) + 340x, which must be at least 3,460, so 90(x + 5) + 340x ≥ 3,460.
reasons: subtracted the difference from the earlier price instead of adding it
read the limit as a maximum instead of a minimum
subtracted the difference from the earlier price and read the limit as a maximum instead of a minimum

module1.rationale: The two brackets multiply to 2n² + 12n − 32 only when r makes the constant term −32.
reasons: reported the constant term of the expression instead
divided the constant term by the leading coefficient
reported the constant already inside the first bracket

module2_lower.rationale: From circumference = 40π, the radius is 20, so the diameter is 40.

module2_lower.stem: Which of the following is equivalent to w² + 14w − 15?
module2_lower.rationale: Half of 14 is 7, and (w + 7)² already carries 49, so −64 is what is left to reach −15.
reasons: halved the middle coefficient with the wrong sign and corrected the wrong way too
added the correction instead of subtracting it
halved the middle coefficient but changed its sign

module2_lower.stem: An angle has a measure of 7π/12 radians. What is the measure of the angle, in degrees?
module2_lower.rationale: Multiplying by 180/π gives (7π/12)(180/π) = 105 degrees.

module2_lower.stem: Which of the following is an equivalent form of √(16x⁴y⁴)/x⁴ ?
module2_lower.rationale: √(16x⁴y⁴) is 4x²y², and dividing by x⁴ subtracts 4 from the exponent of x.
reasons: used the square root of the coefficient as the root's index and divided each exponent by it
subtracted the exponents the wrong way round and dropped the minus sign
halved the coefficient instead of taking its square root, and never divided by x⁴

module2_lower.rationale: (2n + 3.5)² is 4n² + 14n + 12.25, and every term of the second bracket is then subtracted.
reasons: doubled each term instead of squaring the binomial, so the middle term never appeared
subtracted the two constant terms the wrong way round
doubled each term instead of squaring and then added the two constants rather than subtracting

module2_lower.stem: A cargo helicopter delivers only 110-pound packages and 210-pound packages. For each delivery trip, the cargo helicopter must carry at least 8 packages, and the total weight of the packages can be at most 1,550 pounds. What is the maximum number of 210-pound packages that the cargo helicopter can carry per trip?
module2_lower.rationale: Carrying 8 of the lighter packages weighs 880 pounds, and each swap to a heavier one adds 100 pounds. The cap leaves 670 pounds to spend on swaps, so at most 6 of the packages can be the heavier kind.
reasons: divided the weight left over by the heavier package rather than by the difference between the two
stopped one swap short of the weight the load allows
rounded the number of swaps up instead of down

module2_lower.rationale: Both sides carry x², and what is left is 24x = 6, so x = 1/4.
reasons: solved for the wrong sign of x
cancelled both sides entirely and concluded that x is zero

module2_lower.stem: A square and a circle have the same area. If the area of the circle is 484π, what is the perimeter of the square?
module2_lower.rationale: The circle has area pi(22)^2 = 484π; a square of that area has side 22√π, so its perimeter is 88√π.
reasons: found the area as πr, forgetting to square the radius, and then took the square root
used the radius as the side length
used πr, forgetting to square the radius or take the root

module2_lower.stem: A number x is at least 11 more than 5 times the value of y. If the value of y is 12, what is the least possible value of x?
module2_lower.rationale: The condition is x ≥ 5y + 11, and with y = 12 the right side is 71, so the least value x can take is 71.

module2_upper.stem: A clothing store is having a sale on shirts and pants. During the sale, the cost of each shirt is $12 and the cost of each pair of pants is $25. Valentina can spend less than $220 at the store. If Valentina buys x shirts and y pants, which of the following must be true?

module2_upper.stem: Which of the following is equivalent to (5y³ − 9y² + 9y + 5) − (5y³ + 8y² + 2y + 2) ?

For each delivery trip, the cargo helicopter must carry at least 11 packages, and the total weight of the packages can be at most 2,100 pounds. What is the maximum number of 220-pound packages that the cargo helicopter can carry per trip?
module2_upper.rationale: Carrying 11 of the lighter packages weighs 1,980 pounds, and each swap to a heavier one adds 40 pounds. The cap leaves 120 pounds to spend on swaps, so at most 3 of the packages can be the heavier kind.
reasons: stopped one swap short of the weight the load allows
rounded the number of swaps up instead of down
divided the whole weight allowance by the heavier package and ignored the smallest number of packages

module2_upper.stem:
y = 5x² − x − 8
7x + y = −1
Which ordered pair (x, y) is a solution to the given system of equations?
module2_upper.rationale: Putting the line into y = 5x² − x − 8 leaves a quadratic in x whose solutions are −3/5 − (2/5)√11 and −3/5 + (2/5)√11, and the line then gives y = 16/5 + (14/5)√11 and 16/5 − (14/5)√11.
reasons: lost the sign of the x-coordinate
lost the sign of the y-coordinate
wrote the two coordinates the wrong way round

module2_upper.stem: A number x is at most 4 less than 7 times the value of y. If the value of y is −11, what is the greatest possible value of x?
module2_upper.rationale: The condition is x ≤ 7y − 4, and with y = −11 the right side is −81, so the greatest value x can take is −81.

module2_upper.stem: The box plots summarize the masses, in kilograms, of two groups of gazelles. Based on the box plots, which of the following statements must be true?
choices: The median mass of group 1 is less than the median mass of group 2.
The mean mass of group 1 is greater than the mean mass of group 2.
The mean mass of group 1 is less than the mean mass of group 2.
The median mass of group 1 is greater than the median mass of group 2.

The mean mass of group 1 is greater than the mean mass of group 2.

module2_upper.stem: A local transit company sells a monthly pass for $70 that allows an unlimited number of trips of any length. Tickets for individual trips cost $3.00, $4.00, or $5.00, depending on the length of the trip. What is the minimum number of trips per month for which a monthly pass could cost less than purchasing individual tickets for trips?
module2_upper.rationale: The condition is 5n > 70. With n = 15 the ticket cost is $75.00, which meets it, and with n = 14 it is $70.00, which does not, so the least whole number that works is 15.

module2_upper.topic_name: One-Variable Data: Distributions and Measures of Centre and Spread
module2_upper.stem: Each of the following frequency tables represents a data set. Which data set has the greatest mean?
module2_upper.rationale: Only one table gives the larger values the larger frequencies; its mean is 905/11, against 80, 80, and 80 for the others.
reasons: holds the most values of any table, chosen by comparing totals rather than means
gives the greatest value its largest frequency, but gives the least value the same one, so its mean is still the middle value
every value occurs equally often, so its mean is the middle of the values, not the greatest mean here

module2_upper.stem:
2x + 5y = 29
6x + 15y = 87
For each real number r, which of the following points lies on the graph of each equation in the xy-plane for the given system?
module2_upper.rationale: The second equation is the first multiplied by 3, so the two draw the same line and any point on it will do. Letting y be r and solving 2x + 5y = 29 for x gives every such point at once.
reasons: solved the equation for x but wrote that expression as the y-coordinate
solved for y but kept the sign of the x term, which changes the line
divided r by the multiplier between the two equations and used the two right-hand sides as the shifts

module2_upper.topic_name: One-Variable Data: Distributions and Measures of Centre and Spread
module2_upper.stem: The mean score of 18 players in a basketball game was 46 points. If the highest individual score is removed, the mean score of the remaining 17 players becomes 43 points. What was the highest score?
module2_upper.rationale: The 18 values total 828 and the 17 that remain total 731, a difference of 97.
reasons: reported how far the mean fell, not the value that was taken away
swapped the two counts, using one fewer for the original group
subtracted 18 times the new mean instead of 17 times

module2_upper.stem: The graph of 8x − 3y = 20 in the xy-plane has an x-intercept at (a, 0) and a y-intercept at (0, b), where a and b are constants. What is the value of b/a?
module2_upper.rationale: a is 20 divided by 8 and b is 20 divided by −3, so dividing b by a cancels the 20 and leaves the two coefficients.
reasons: divided a by b instead of b by a
divided a by b and changed the sign
changed the sign of the ratio

module2_upper.stem: Point O is the center of the circle above, and the measure of angle OAB is 35°. If the length of OF is 24, what is the measure, in degrees, of angle AOB?

doubled the base angle instead of subtracting twice it from 180
subtracted the base angle from 180 only once

module2_upper.stem:
⁶√(50n)(⁹√(50n))²
For what value of x is the given expression equivalent to (50n)^(15x), where n > 1?
module2_upper.rationale: The two roots give exponents 1/6 and 2/9, which add to 7/18, and that has to equal 15x.

module2_upper.stem: One of the factors of 2x³ + 34x² + 132x is x + b, where b is a positive constant. What is the smallest possible value of b?
module2_upper.rationale: 2x³ + 34x² + 132x is 2x(x + 6)(x + 11), so b is 6 or 11.

module2_upper.stem: Which of the following is equivalent to (n² + 2n + 7)/(n + 5) ?
module2_upper.rationale: n² + 2n + 7 is (n + 5)(n − 3) + 22, and only 22 is left over.
reasons: used the divisor's constant with the wrong sign when finding the quotient
subtracted the divisor's constant from the remainder instead of multiplying by it
used the divisor's constant with the wrong sign, and then added the quotient's constant to the remainder instead of multiplying it by the divisor's root

module1.stem:
|x + 9| = 12
What is the positive solution to the given equation?
module1.rationale: The quantity inside the bars is 12 or −12, so x = 3 or x = −21.

module1.stem: Devon plans to rent a bicycle. The bicycle rental costs $40 per hour, and Devon will also have to pay for a helmet rental that costs $25. Devon wants to spend no more than $340 for the rental and the helmet rental. If the bicycle rental is available only for a whole number of hours, what is the maximum number of hours for which Devon can rent the bicycle?
module1.rationale: The condition is 25 + 40n ≤ 340. With n = 7 the cost is $305.00, which meets it, and with n = 8 it is $345.00, which does not, so the greatest whole number that works is 7.

module1.stem: Point O is the center of a circle, and points R and S lie on the circle. The measure of angle ROS is 55°. What is the measure, in degrees, of major arc RS?
module1.rationale: The two arcs make a full turn, so the major arc measures 360 − 55 = 305 degrees.

module1.stem:
w = 6cy
The given equation relates the distinct positive numbers w, c, and y. Which equation correctly expresses c in terms of w and y?
module1.rationale: Multiplying both sides of w = 6cy by whatever divides c and dividing by whatever multiplies it gives c = w/(6y).
reasons: wrote the whole right-hand side upside down
kept the coefficient on the side it started on instead of moving it across
turned the fraction upside down

module1.stem: Which of the following is an equivalent form of 256y² − 1156 ?
module1.rationale: 256 is 16² and 1156 is 34², so the expression is y times 16 all squared minus 34 squared.
reasons: halved the two square roots instead of taking them
used the same sign in both brackets, which squares the first bracket instead
halved the two square roots and used the same sign in both brackets

module1.stem: For a 3-week period in a town in Illinois, the lowest recorded temperature was 42 degrees Fahrenheit (°F) and the highest recorded temperature was 96°F. Which inequality is true for any recorded temperature t, in °F, in this town for this 3-week period?
module1.rationale: Every recorded value is at least the smallest, 42, and at most the largest, 96; both were recorded, so both ends belong to the range and 42 ≤ t ≤ 96.
reasons: kept only the smallest recorded value and read it as a cap rather than as the bottom of the range
kept only the largest recorded value and read it as a floor rather than as the top of the range
used the largest recorded value as the bottom of the range and the sum of the two as the top

module1.stem: A certain rhinoceros weighs 260 pounds at birth and gains more than 1 but less than 3 pounds per day during its first year. Which of the following inequalities represents all possible weights w, in pounds, for the rhinoceros 285 days after birth?
module1.rationale: The smallest the quantity can be is 260 + 285(1) = 545, and the largest is 260 + 285(3) = 1,115; the multiplier is positive, so the ends keep their order and 545 < w < 1,115.
reasons: left the birth weight out of both ends of the range
multiplied the birth weight by each end of the range instead of adding the amount the rate builds up
added the birth weight at the top of the range but not at the bottom

module1.stem: A circle has a circumference of 52π feet. What is the radius, in feet, of the circle?
module1.rationale: From circumference = 52π, the radius is 26, so the radius is 26.

module1.topic_name: One-Variable Data: Distributions and Measures of Centre and Spread
module1.stem: If a is the mean and b is the median of five consecutive integers, what is the value of |a − b| ?
module1.rationale: Consecutive integers are evenly spaced about their middle value, so the mean and the median are the same number.

module1.stem: Which of the following expressions is equivalent to (p + q/4)² ?
module1.rationale: (p + q/4)² is p² plus twice p·q/4 plus (q/4)², and squaring a fraction squares its denominator too.
reasons: left out the middle term of the square
forgot to double the middle term and squared only the numerator of the fraction
left out the middle term and squared only the numerator of the fraction

module1.stem: A model estimates that whales from the genus Balaenoptera travel 46 to 53 miles in the ocean each day during their migration. Based on this model, which inequality represents the estimated total number of miles, x, one of these whales could travel in 28 days of its migration?
module1.rationale: Each of the 28 days adds between 46 and 53 miles, so the smallest total is (46)(28) and the largest is (53)(28); multiplying by a positive number keeps the two ends in order, so (46)(28) ≤ x ≤ (53)(28).
reasons: divided by the quantity that should have been multiplied, which also turns the two ends round
added the two quantities instead of multiplying them
subtracted the two quantities instead of multiplying them

module1.stem: A cargo helicopter delivers only 120-pound packages and 150-pound packages. For each delivery trip, the cargo helicopter must carry at least 14 packages, and the total weight of the packages can be at most 2,050 pounds. What is the maximum number of 150-pound packages that the cargo helicopter can carry per trip?
module1.rationale: Carrying 14 of the lighter packages weighs 1,680 pounds, and each swap to a heavier one adds 30 pounds. The cap leaves 370 pounds to spend on swaps, so at most 12 of the packages can be the heavier kind.
reasons: divided the weight left over by the heavier package rather than by the difference between the two
stopped one swap short of the weight the load allows
rounded the number of swaps up instead of down

module1.stem: Which of the following expressions is equivalent to (−2j³ − 6j² + j + 1) + (5j³ − 4j² + 8j + 7)?
module1.rationale: Like terms are collected power by power.
reasons: multiplied the coefficients of the like terms instead of adding them
added the exponents as well as the coefficients
added every coefficient and every exponent as if all the terms were alike

module1.stem: The graph in the xy-plane models the possible combinations of length x, in meters (m), and width y, in meters, for a rectangle with a perimeter of 38 m. Which statement is the best interpretation of the point (13, 6) in this context?
choices: The length is 13 m less than the perimeter, and the width is 6 m less than the perimeter.
The length is 13 m, and the width is 6 m.
The length is 6 m less than the perimeter, and the width is 13 m less than the perimeter.
The length is 6 m, and the width is 13 m.
latex: The length is 13 m less than the perimeter, and the width is 6 m less than the perimeter.
The length is 13 m, and the width is 6 m.
The length is 6 m less than the perimeter, and the width is 13 m less than the perimeter.
The length is 6 m, and the width is 13 m.

module2_lower.rationale: The coefficients multiply and the exponents of v and of w each add, giving 84v²w².
reasons: multiplied the coefficients but added none of the exponents
added the three coefficients instead of multiplying them
added the exponents of v but left w alone

module2_lower.stem: Which expression is equivalent to (p + q/5)²?
module2_lower.rationale: (p + q/5)² is p² plus twice p·q/5 plus (q/5)², and squaring a fraction squares its denominator too.
reasons: forgot to double the middle term and squared only the numerator of the fraction
left out the middle term and squared only the numerator of the fraction
left out the middle term of the square

module2_lower.stem: A certain rhinoceros weighs 210 pounds at birth and gains more than 5 but less than 8 pounds per day during its first year. Which of the following inequalities represents all possible weights w, in pounds, for the rhinoceros 340 days after birth?
module2_lower.rationale: The smallest the quantity can be is 210 + 340(5) = 1,910, and the largest is 210 + 340(8) = 2,930; the multiplier is positive, so the ends keep their order and 1,910 < w < 2,930.
reasons: multiplied the birth weight by each end of the range instead of adding the amount the rate builds up
left the birth weight out of both ends of the range
added the birth weight at the top of the range but not at the bottom

module2_lower.stem:
(x + 4)(x + 8) = (x − 4)(x − 8) + 32
Which of the following is a solution to the given equation?
module2_lower.rationale: Both sides carry x², and what is left is 24x = 32, so x = 4/3.
reasons: solved for the wrong sign of x
cancelled both sides entirely and concluded that x is zero
forgot that the x terms appear twice over

module2_lower.stem: A number x is at most 9 more than 5 times the value of y. If the value of y is −11, what is the greatest possible value of x?
module2_lower.rationale: The condition is x ≤ 5y + 9, and with y = −11 the right side is −46, so the greatest value x can take is −46.

module2_lower.rationale: The condition is 0.024n ≤ 0.55. With n = 22 the current is 0.528, which meets it, and with n = 23 it is 0.552, which does not, so the greatest whole number that works is 22.

When p = 1, Alice has a maximum heart rate. It is recommended that p be between 0.4 and 0.6 for Alice when training. Which of the following inequalities describes Alice's target training heart rate?
module2_upper.rationale: The smallest the quantity can be is 75 + 140(0.4) = 131, and the largest is 75 + 140(0.6) = 159; the multiplier is positive, so the ends keep their order and 131 ≤ H ≤ 159.
reasons: multiplied the resting heart rate by each end of the range instead of adding the amount the rate builds up
left the resting heart rate out of both ends of the range

module2_upper.rationale: The condition is x ≤ 6y − 7, and with y = 1 the right side is −1, so the greatest value x can take is −1.

module2_upper.stem:
f(w) = w³ − 100w
g(w) = w² − 9w − 10
Which of the following expressions is equivalent to f(w)/g(w), for w > 10 ?
module2_upper.rationale: w³ − 100w is w(w − 10)(w + 10) and w² − 9w − 10 is (w − 10)(w + 1), so only w − 10 cancels.
reasons: cancelled everything in the numerator against the denominator
cancelled the w in front as well as the shared bracket
cancelled the wrong bracket and kept the one the denominator shares

module2_upper.stem:
(n² − c)/(n − b)
In the expression above, b and c are positive integers. If the expression is equivalent to n + b and n ≠ b, which of the following could be the value of c ?
module2_upper.rationale: (n − b)(n + b) is n² − b², so c has to be a perfect square.
reasons: used b(b + 1) in place of b²
kept the middle terms of the expansion instead of letting them cancel
left three copies of b behind when expanding

module2_upper.stem:
y = 3x² − 8x − 12
y + 11 = 0
How many solutions are there to the system of equations above?
module2_upper.rationale: Setting the two right-hand sides equal gives 3x² − 8x − 1 = 0, whose discriminant is 76, so the graphs share exactly two points.
reasons: multiplied the number of solutions of the quadratic by the two branches of the curve
read the sign of the discriminant the wrong way round, and concluded that the curve never meets the axis
counted the two square roots of a positive number as a single solution

module1.rationale: The quantity inside the bars is 25 or −25, so x = 30 or x = −20.

module1.rationale: Putting x = 0 wipes out the term in x, and what is left is the constant term.

module1.stem: Julissa needs at least 280 hours of flight time to get a private pilot certification. If Julissa already has 90 hours of flight time, what is the minimum number of additional hours of flight time Julissa needs to get a private pilot certification?
module1.rationale: The condition is 90 + n ≥ 280. With n = 190 the flight time is 280, which meets it, and with n = 189 it is 279, which does not, so the least whole number that works is 190.
reasons: reported the amount already accounted for rather than what is still needed
left the amount already accounted for out of the subtraction
added the two given amounts instead of subtracting them

module1.stem:
H = 120p + 60
The formula above shows the relationship between Renata's target heart rate H, in beats per minute (bpm), and the intensity level p of different activities. When p = 0, Renata has a resting heart rate. When p = 1, Renata has a maximum heart rate. It is recommended that p be between 0.55 and 0.7 for Renata when training. Which of the following inequalities describes Renata's target training heart rate?
module1.rationale: The smallest the quantity can be is 60 + 120(0.55) = 126, and the largest is 60 + 120(0.7) = 144; the multiplier is positive, so the ends keep their order and 126 ≤ H ≤ 144.
reasons: multiplied the resting heart rate by each end of the range instead of adding the amount the rate builds up
left the resting heart rate out of both ends of the range
added the resting heart rate at the top of the range but not at the bottom

module1.stem: Which of the following is equivalent to w² + 14w − 3 ?
module1.rationale: Half of 14 is 7, and (w + 7)² already carries 49, so −52 is what is left to reach −3.
reasons: added the correction instead of subtracting it
halved the middle coefficient but changed its sign

module1.stem: The length of a rectangle is 40 inches and the width is x inches. The perimeter is at most 240 inches. Which inequality represents this situation?
module1.rationale: The perimeter is two widths and two lengths, which is 2x + 80, and that must be at most 240, so 2x + 80 ≤ 240.
reasons: counted the length once instead of twice when writing the perimeter
read the limit as a minimum instead of a maximum
counted the length once instead of twice and read the limit as a minimum instead of a maximum

module1.stem: A cargo helicopter delivers only 60-pound packages and 220-pound packages. For each delivery trip, the cargo helicopter must carry at least 14 packages, and the total weight of the packages can be at most 2,550 pounds. What is the maximum number of 220-pound packages that the cargo helicopter can carry per trip?
module1.rationale: Carrying 14 of the lighter packages weighs 840 pounds, and each swap to a heavier one adds 160 pounds. The cap leaves 1,710 pounds to spend on swaps, so at most 10 of the packages can be the heavier kind.
reasons: divided the weight left over by the heavier package rather than by the difference between the two
stopped one swap short of the weight the load allows
rounded the number of swaps up instead of down

module1.rationale: u⁻³v⁴w⁴ multiplies each term inside the parentheses, and the exponents of each variable add.
reasons: multiplied only the first term inside the parentheses by the monomial
left v out of both products because it is missing from one factor of each
kept only the variables that both factors carry, dropping v from the first product and u from the second

module1.stem:
f(z) = z³ − 121z
g(z) = z² − 2z − 99
Which of the following expressions is equivalent to f(z)/g(z), for z > 11 ?
module1.rationale: z³ − 121z is z(z − 11)(z + 11) and z² − 2z − 99 is (z − 11)(z + 9), so only z − 11 cancels.
reasons: cancelled the z in front as well as the shared bracket
cancelled everything in the numerator against the denominator
cancelled the wrong bracket and kept the one the denominator shares

module2_lower.stem: During spring migration, an arctic tern traveled a minimum of 31 miles and a maximum of 81 miles between stopover locations. Which inequality represents this situation, where d is a possible distance, in miles, this arctic tern traveled between stopover locations during spring migration?
module2_lower.rationale: Every recorded value is at least the smallest, 31, and at most the largest, 81; both were recorded, so both ends belong to the range and 31 ≤ d ≤ 81.
reasons: used the largest recorded value as the bottom of the range and the sum of the two as the top
kept only the largest recorded value and read it as a floor rather than as the top of the range
kept only the smallest recorded value and read it as a cap rather than as the bottom of the range

module2_lower.stem: A geologist estimates that the volume of a slab of limestone is greater than 22.2 cubic feet but less than 27.7 cubic feet. The geologist also estimates that the slab of limestone weighs 130 pounds per cubic foot of volume. Which inequality represents this situation, where x represents the estimated total weight, in pounds, of the slab of limestone?
module2_lower.rationale: Each cubic foot weighs 130 pounds, so the smallest total is 130(22.2) and the largest is 130(27.7); multiplying by a positive number keeps the two ends in order, so 130(22.2) < x < 130(27.7).
reasons: added the two quantities instead of multiplying them
divided by the quantity that should have been multiplied, which also turns the two ends round
subtracted the two quantities instead of multiplying them

module2_lower.stem: A club selected 350 fans at random from a list of the fans who hold a season ticket. The 350 fans were shown the design for a new stadium and then asked whether they approved or disapproved of it. Of those surveyed, 92% said they disapproved of the design. Which of the following inferences can appropriately be drawn from this survey result?
choices: At least 92% of fans who watch the game on television will disapprove of the design.
Most fans who hold a season ticket will disapprove of the design.
Most fans who do not hold a season ticket will approve of the design.
Most fans who hold a season ticket will approve of the design.
latex: At least 92% of fans who watch the game on television will disapprove of the design.
Most fans who hold a season ticket will disapprove of the design.
Most fans who do not hold a season ticket will approve of the design.
Most fans who hold a season ticket will approve of the design.
module2_lower.rationale: The fans were selected at random from fans who hold a season ticket, so only a claim about that group is licensed; 92% of one sample estimates the population rather than fixing it, so only “most” is supported.
reasons: generalized past the sampling frame, and repeated the sample's percentage as if it held exactly
swapped the group the sample came from for its complement, and the response with it
read the minority response of the sample as its majority response

module2_lower.stem: A clothing store is having a sale on shirts and pants. During the sale, the cost of each shirt is $45 and the cost of each pair of pants is $20. Sofia can spend at most $400 at the store. If Sofia buys x shirts and y pants, which of the following must be true?
module2_lower.rationale: x shirts at $45 each cost 45x, and y pants at $20 each cost 20y; the two together have to come to at most $400, so 45x + 20y ≤ 400.
reasons: attached each price to the other kind of item
attached each price to the other kind of item and read the limit as a minimum instead of a maximum
read the limit as a minimum instead of a maximum

module2_lower.rationale: The quantity inside the bars is 25 or −25, so x = 22 or x = −28.

module2_lower.stem:
(4z² + 2z − 1) − (4z² + 5z + 9)
Which of the following is equivalent to the expression above?
module2_lower.rationale: Like terms are collected power by power, and the minus sign in front of (4z² + 5z + 9) applies to every term inside it.
reasons: applied the minus sign to its own answer's lower terms instead of to the second polynomial
let the minus sign reach only the middle term of the second polynomial
added the second polynomial instead of subtracting it

module2_lower.stem:
196z² − 676
Which of the following expressions is equivalent to the expression above?
module2_lower.rationale: 196 is 14² and 676 is 26², so the expression is z times 14 all squared minus 26 squared.
reasons: halved the two square roots instead of taking them
halved the two square roots and used the same sign in both brackets
used the same sign in both brackets, which squares the first bracket instead

module2_lower.stem: Which of the following expressions is equivalent to (x + y/4)²?
module2_lower.rationale: (x + y/4)² is x² plus twice x·y/4 plus (y/4)², and squaring a fraction squares its denominator too.
reasons: left out the middle term of the square
forgot to double the middle term and squared only the numerator of the fraction
left out the middle term and squared only the numerator of the fraction

module2_lower.stem: A circle has center O, and points A and C lie on the circle. The measure of arc AC is 60° and the length of arc AC is 19 feet. What is the circumference, in feet, of the circle?
module2_lower.rationale: The arc is 60/360 of the circle, so the circumference is 19 ÷ (60/360) = 114.

module2_lower.stem: Which of the following is equivalent to k² + 14k − 2 ?
module2_lower.rationale: Half of 14 is 7, and (k + 7)² already carries 49, so −51 is what is left to reach −2.
reasons: halved the middle coefficient but changed its sign
added the correction instead of subtracting it
halved the middle coefficient with the wrong sign and corrected the wrong way too

module2_lower.stem: What is the measure, in radians, of an angle that measures 620°?
module2_lower.rationale: Multiplying by π/180 gives 620(π/180) = 31π/9 radians.
reasons: inverted the fraction before converting
divided by 360 instead of 180
divided by 90 instead of 180

module2_lower.stem:
(x + 6)(x + 8) = (x − 6)(x − 8) − 35
Which of the following is a solution to the given equation?
module2_lower.rationale: Both sides carry x², and what is left is 28x = −35, so x = −5/4.
reasons: forgot that the x terms appear twice over
cancelled both sides entirely and concluded that x is zero
solved for the wrong sign of x

module2_lower.stem:
y = 2x² + 6x + 4
y = −5x − 11
A solution to the given system of equations is (x, y). Which of the following is a possible value of xy ?
module2_lower.rationale: Putting the line into y = 2x² + 6x + 4 leaves a quadratic in x whose solutions are −3 and −5/2, and the line then gives y = 4 and 3/2.
reasons: reported x rather than the product asked for
reported y rather than the product asked for
squared one coordinate instead of multiplying the two

module2_lower.stem: A certain elephant weighs 220 pounds at birth and gains more than 3 but less than 7 pounds per day during its first year. Which of the following inequalities represents all possible weights w, in pounds, for the elephant 315 days after birth?
module2_lower.rationale: The smallest the quantity can be is 220 + 315(3) = 1,165, and the largest is 220 + 315(7) = 2,425; the multiplier is positive, so the ends keep their order and 1,165 < w < 2,425.
reasons: added the birth weight at the top of the range but not at the bottom
multiplied the birth weight by each end of the range instead of adding the amount the rate builds up
left the birth weight out of both ends of the range

module2_lower.stem:
(x + 5)(x + 4) = 0
What is the product of the solutions to the given equation?
module2_lower.rationale: Each bracket gives a solution, so they are −5 and −4, and their product is 20.
reasons: added the solutions instead of multiplying them
added the solutions and kept the signs printed in the brackets
near-miss arithmetic slip

module2_lower.stem: A number x is at most 13 more than 2 times the value of y. If the value of y is 8, what is the greatest possible value of x?
module2_lower.rationale: The condition is x ≤ 2y + 13, and with y = 8 the right side is 29, so the greatest value x can take is 29.

module2_lower.stem: The line with the equation (1/6)x + (4/7)y = 7 is graphed in the xy-plane. What is the x-coordinate of the x-intercept of the line?
module2_lower.rationale: On the x-axis y is zero, so the term in y drops out and the term in x has to account for the whole right-hand side by itself.

module2_upper.stem: What is the value of sin 157π/3 ?
module2_upper.rationale: 157π/3 and π/3 differ by whole turns, so sin 157π/3 = sin π/3 = √3/2.
reasons: gave the cosine of the angle instead
used the 45-degree reference value
dropped the 2 in the denominator of the reference value

module2_upper.stem: During spring migration, a monarch butterfly traveled a minimum of 57 miles and a maximum of 74 miles between stopover locations. Which inequality represents this situation, where d is a possible distance, in miles, this monarch butterfly traveled between stopover locations during spring migration?
module2_upper.rationale: Every recorded value is at least the smallest, 57, and at most the largest, 74; both were recorded, so both ends belong to the range and 57 ≤ d ≤ 74.
reasons: used the largest recorded value as the bottom of the range and the sum of the two as the top
kept only the smallest recorded value and read it as a cap rather than as the bottom of the range
kept only the largest recorded value and read it as a floor rather than as the top of the range

module2_upper.stem: Maria needs at least 290 hours of flight time to get a private pilot certification. If Maria already has 42 hours of flight time, what is the minimum number of additional hours of flight time Maria needs to get a private pilot certification?
module2_upper.rationale: The condition is 42 + n ≥ 290. With n = 248 the flight time is 290, which meets it, and with n = 247 it is 289, which does not, so the least whole number that works is 248.
reasons: reported the amount already accounted for rather than what is still needed
left the amount already accounted for out of the subtraction
added the two given amounts instead of subtracting them

module2_upper.stem: Which of the following expressions is equivalent to x² + 4x − 11 ?
module2_upper.rationale: Half of 4 is 2, and (x + 2)² already carries 4, so −15 is what is left to reach −11.
reasons: added the correction instead of subtracting it
halved the middle coefficient with the wrong sign and corrected the wrong way too
halved the middle coefficient but changed its sign

module2_upper.stem: In a circle with a circumference of 25 feet, central angle JOK measures 144°. What is the length, in feet, of arc JK?
module2_upper.rationale: The arc takes 144/360 of the circle, so its length is (144/360)(25) = 10.

module2_upper.stem: Which expression is equivalent to (p − 3q)(5p − 2q) − 14q(−4p + 3q)?
module2_upper.rationale: The two brackets multiply term by term, and −14q then multiplies both terms of (−4p + 3q).
reasons: added the terms instead of multiplying the brackets out
used the minus sign in front of the second product twice -- once inside it and once again when combining
multiplied the first brackets out but kept the sign of the last term of the second product

gave the major arc instead of the whole circumference

module2_upper.stem: Which of the following is equivalent to z² − 19 ?
module2_upper.rationale: 19 is not a perfect square, but it is still √19 squared, so the expression is a difference of two squares.
reasons: used the same negative sign in both brackets
looked for two whole numbers multiplying to −19 instead of taking a square root
used the same sign in both brackets, which gives a square rather than a difference of squares

module2_upper.stem: Which of the following expressions is equivalent to (x⁻⁶y⁵z⁴)(x²z⁶ + y⁸z⁻⁷) ?
module2_upper.rationale: x⁻⁶y⁵z⁴ multiplies each term inside the parentheses, and the exponents of each variable add.
reasons: kept only the variables that both factors carry, dropping y from the first product and x from the second
multiplied only the first term inside the parentheses by the monomial
left y out of both products because it is missing from one factor of each

module2_upper.stem: A certain giraffe weighs 130 pounds at birth and gains more than 5 but less than 9 pounds per day during its first year. Which of the following inequalities represents all possible weights w, in pounds, for the giraffe 330 days after birth?
module2_upper.rationale: The smallest the quantity can be is 130 + 330(5) = 1,780, and the largest is 130 + 330(9) = 3,100; the multiplier is positive, so the ends keep their order and 1,780 < w < 3,100.
reasons: left the birth weight out of both ends of the range
multiplied the birth weight by each end of the range instead of adding the amount the rate builds up
added the birth weight at the top of the range but not at the bottom

module2_upper.stem:
y = (x + 7)²
y = −4x + 10
Which ordered pair (x, y) is a solution to the given system of equations?
module2_upper.rationale: Putting the line into y = (x + 7)² leaves a quadratic in x whose solutions are −9 − √42 and −9 + √42, and the line then gives y = 46 + 4√42 and 46 − 4√42.
reasons: lost the sign of the y-coordinate
wrote the two coordinates the wrong way round
lost the sign of the x-coordinate

module2_upper.stem: A number x is at most 13 less than 9 times the value of y. If the value of y is −7, what is the greatest possible value of x?
module2_upper.rationale: The condition is x ≤ 9y − 13, and with y = −7 the right side is −76, so the greatest value x can take is −76.

module2_upper.topic_name: One-Variable Data: Distributions and Measures of Centre and Spread
module2_upper.stem:
24, 24, 24, 24, 25, 25, 31, 31, 31, 31
Which frequency table correctly represents the data listed?
module2_upper.rationale: 24 appears 4 times, 25 appears 2 times, 31 appears 4 times.
reasons: swapped the two columns, reading each count as a data value
multiplied each value by its count and then swapped the columns
multiplied each value by how many times it appears instead of counting the appearances

In one week, Avery earned a total of s dollars for working at the two part-time jobs. The graph above represents all possible combinations of numbers of hours Avery could have worked at the two jobs to earn s dollars. What is the value of s ?

module2_upper.topic_name: One-Variable Data: Distributions and Measures of Centre and Spread
module2_upper.stem: The mean score of 6 players in a basketball game was 12 points. If the highest individual score is removed, the mean score of the remaining 5 players becomes 10.5 points. What was the highest score?
module2_upper.rationale: The 6 values total 72 and the 5 that remain total 52.5, a difference of 19.5.
reasons: reported how far the mean fell, not the value that was taken away
multiplied the fall in the mean by one less than the original count
added the two means

module2_upper.stem: The line with the equation (1/6)x + (2/3)y = 2 is graphed in the xy-plane. What is the x-coordinate of the x-intercept of the line?
module2_upper.rationale: On the x-axis y is zero, so the term in y drops out and the term in x has to account for the whole right-hand side by itself.

module2_upper.stem: A botanist selected 100 seedlings at random from the seedlings in a greenhouse and randomly assigned them to two groups. One group was grown under a blue lamp for 3 weeks and the other under the usual lamp. The group grown under the blue lamp put on significantly more stem growth. Which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion from this study?
choices: The blue lamp causes an increase in stem growth for all seedlings of this species.
The blue lamp causes an increase in stem growth for the seedlings in this greenhouse.
The blue lamp causes an increase in stem growth for the 100 seedlings in the study.
There is an association between the blue lamp and an increase in stem growth for all seedlings of this species.
latex: The blue lamp causes an increase in stem growth for all seedlings of this species.
The blue lamp causes an increase in stem growth for the seedlings in this greenhouse.
The blue lamp causes an increase in stem growth for the 100 seedlings in the study.
There is an association between the blue lamp and an increase in stem growth for all seedlings of this species.
module2_upper.rationale: The seedlings were randomly assigned, so the difference between the groups is a cause; they were selected at random from the seedlings in this greenhouse, so the conclusion reaches that group.
reasons: generalized past the seedlings in this greenhouse, the group the seedlings were selected from
kept the conclusion inside the study although the units were selected at random from a whole group
generalized past the seedlings in this greenhouse, the group the seedlings were selected from

module2_upper.stem: How many liters of a 25% saline solution must be added to 2 liters of a 6% saline solution to obtain a 21% saline solution?
module2_upper.rationale: Each liter added carries 25% salt into a blend that is only 21%, a surplus of 4 percentage points, and each of the 2 liters already there is 15 points short; the surpluses have to cancel the shortfalls exactly.

module2_upper.stem: Point O is the center of the circle above, the measure of angle OAB is 35°, and the radius of the circle is 6. What is the measure, in degrees, of angle AOB?

module2_upper.stem: The expression (3j − 24)(19j + 7) is equivalent to the expression aj² + bj + c, where a, b, and c are constants. What is the value of b?
module2_upper.rationale: The middle coefficient is the sum of the two cross products, 3 × 7 and −24 × 19.

module2_upper.stem:
f(t) = t³ − 16t
g(t) = t² − 3t − 4
Which of the following expressions is equivalent to f(t)/g(t), for t > 4 ?
module2_upper.rationale: t³ − 16t is t(t − 4)(t + 4) and t² − 3t − 4 is (t − 4)(t + 1), so only t − 4 cancels.
reasons: cancelled the wrong bracket and kept the one the denominator shares
cancelled the t in front as well as the shared bracket
cancelled everything in the numerator against the denominator

module2_upper.stem:
y = x² + 2x + 3
y − 9x − 14 = 0
How many solutions are there to the system of equations above?
module2_upper.rationale: Setting the two right-hand sides equal gives x² − 7x − 11 = 0, whose discriminant is 93, so the graphs share exactly two points.
reasons: multiplied the number of solutions of the quadratic by the two branches of the curve
counted the two square roots of a positive number as a single solution
read the sign of the discriminant the wrong way round, and concluded that the curve never meets the axis

module1.stem:
|x + 7| = 24
What is the positive solution to the given equation?
module1.rationale: The quantity inside the bars is 24 or −24, so x = 17 or x = −31.

module1.stem: For a 5-week period in a town in Vermont, the lowest recorded temperature was 75 degrees Fahrenheit (°F) and the highest recorded temperature was 114°F. Which inequality is true for any recorded temperature t, in °F, in this town for this 5-week period?
module1.rationale: Every recorded value is at least the smallest, 75, and at most the largest, 114; both were recorded, so both ends belong to the range and 75 ≤ t ≤ 114.
reasons: kept only the smallest recorded value and read it as a cap rather than as the bottom of the range
used the largest recorded value as the bottom of the range and the sum of the two as the top
kept only the largest recorded value and read it as a floor rather than as the top of the range

module1.stem:
9p⁶ − 9p⁵ + 27p
Which of the following is equivalent to the expression above?
module1.rationale: Every term holds at least one p and a factor of 9, so 9p comes out and each exponent drops by one.
reasons: took the common factor out but reduced none of the exponents
took only the variable out and subtracted one from every coefficient instead of dividing by the common factor
attached the powers of the variable to the coefficient instead of to the variable

module1.stem:
−x² − 15x + 9 = 0
How many distinct real solutions are there to the given equation?
module1.rationale: The equation has a discriminant of 261, so it has exactly two real solutions.
reasons: read the equation as an identity, true for every value of x
read the sign of the discriminant the wrong way round, and concluded that the curve never meets the axis
counted the two square roots of a positive number as a single solution

module1.stem: A geologist estimates that the volume of a slab of limestone is greater than 8.1 cubic feet but less than 13.7 cubic feet. The geologist also estimates that the slab of limestone weighs 175 pounds per cubic foot of volume. Which inequality represents this situation, where x represents the estimated total weight, in pounds, of the slab of limestone?
module1.rationale: Each cubic foot weighs 175 pounds, so the smallest total is 175(8.1) and the largest is 175(13.7); multiplying by a positive number keeps the two ends in order, so 175(8.1) < x < 175(13.7).
reasons: subtracted the two quantities instead of multiplying them
divided by the quantity that should have been multiplied, which also turns the two ends round
added the two quantities instead of multiplying them

module1.stem: A certain giraffe weighs 240 pounds at birth and gains more than 7 but less than 12 pounds per day during its first year. Which of the following inequalities represents all possible weights w, in pounds, for the giraffe 270 days after birth?
module1.rationale: The smallest the quantity can be is 240 + 270(7) = 2,130, and the largest is 240 + 270(12) = 3,480; the multiplier is positive, so the ends keep their order and 2,130 < w < 3,480.
reasons: multiplied the birth weight by each end of the range instead of adding the amount the rate builds up
left the birth weight out of both ends of the range
added the birth weight at the top of the range but not at the bottom

module1.stem: The circle shown has center O and a diameter of 22 meters. What is the length, in meters, of arc AB?

reasons: gave the whole circumference instead of the arc
near-miss arithmetic slip

module1.topic_name: One-Variable Data: Distributions and Measures of Centre and Spread
module1.stem:
13, 14, 18, 20, 4, 12, 18, 12, 20, 3, 16, 10, 12, 7, 1, 9, 14, 20, 17, 15
The mean of the list of numbers above is what fraction of the sum of the twenty numbers?
module1.rationale: The mean is the sum divided by 20, so it is one 20th of the sum whatever the numbers are.

module1.stem: The sum of −3p² − 2p − 18 and −2p² + 6p − 20 can be written in the form ap² + bp + c, where a, b, and c are constants. What is the value of a + b + c ?
module1.rationale: Adding like terms gives −5p² + 4p − 38, and a, b and c are its three coefficients.

module1.stem: The length of a rectangle is 30 inches and the width is x inches. The perimeter is at most 120 inches. Which inequality represents this situation?
module1.rationale: The perimeter is two widths and two lengths, which is 2x + 60, and that must be at most 120, so 2x + 60 ≤ 120.
reasons: counted the length once instead of twice when writing the perimeter
read the limit as a minimum instead of a maximum
counted the length once instead of twice and read the limit as a minimum instead of a maximum

module1.stem: A cargo helicopter delivers only 120-pound packages and 230-pound packages. For each delivery trip, the cargo helicopter must carry at least 16 packages, and the total weight of the packages can be at most 2,550 pounds. What is the maximum number of 230-pound packages that the cargo helicopter can carry per trip?
module1.rationale: Carrying 16 of the lighter packages weighs 1,920 pounds, and each swap to a heavier one adds 110 pounds. The cap leaves 630 pounds to spend on swaps, so at most 5 of the packages can be the heavier kind.
reasons: stopped one swap short of the weight the load allows
rounded the number of swaps up instead of down
divided the whole weight allowance by the heavier package and ignored the smallest number of packages

module1.stem: Which of the following expressions is equivalent to (4t + 4)² − (t + 5) + 3(t + 2)?
module1.rationale: (4t + 4)² is 16t² + 32t + 16, and the minus sign in front of the second bracket reaches its constant too.
reasons: left out the middle term of the square and did not change the sign of the subtracted constant
did not change the sign of the constant in the bracket that is subtracted
left out the middle term of the square

module1.stem: A moving truck can tow a trailer if the combined weight of the trailer and the boxes it contains is no more than 2,400 pounds. What is the maximum number of boxes this truck can tow in a trailer with a weight of 750 pounds if each box weighs 120 pounds?
module1.rationale: The condition is 750 + 120n ≤ 2,400. With n = 13 the combined weight is 2,310, which meets it, and with n = 14 it is 2,430, which does not, so the greatest whole number that works is 13.
reasons: near-miss arithmetic slip
rounded the quotient up instead of down
left the fixed charge out of the total

module1.topic_name: One-Variable Data: Distributions and Measures of Centre and Spread
module1.stem:
16, 16, 16, 16, 26, 26, 26, 26, 30, 30, 30
Which frequency table correctly represents the data listed?
module1.rationale: 16 appears 4 times, 26 appears 4 times, 30 appears 3 times.
reasons: multiplied each value by its count and then swapped the columns
swapped the two columns, reading each count as a data value
multiplied each value by how many times it appears instead of counting the appearances

module1.stem: If √(z³)/⁶√(z⁵) = z^(a/b) for all positive values of z, what is the value of a/b ?
module1.rationale: The two radicals are z^(3/2) and z^(5/6), and dividing subtracts the exponents.

module1.stem: A number x is at least 11 less than 4 times the value of y. If the value of y is −2, what is the least possible value of x?
module1.rationale: The condition is x ≥ 4y − 11, and with y = −2 the right side is −19, so the least value x can take is −19.

module1.stem: Point O is the center of the circle above, the measure of angle OMN is 15°, and the radius of the circle is 2. What is the length of arc MN ?
module1.figure: <svg viewBox="0 0 216 216" width="216" height="216" role="img" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><style>.ax{stroke:currentColor;stroke-width:1.4;fill:none}.gr{stroke:currentColor;stroke-width:.5;opacity:.28}.pt{fill:currentColor}.sg{stroke:currentColor;stroke-width:1.4;fill:none}.lb{fill:currentColor;font:11px ui-sans-serif,system-ui,sans-serif}.it{fill:currentColor;font:italic 13px ui-serif,Georgia,serif}</style><circle class="ax" cx="108" cy="108" r="76"/><line class="sg" x1="34.59" y1="88.33" x2="181.41" y2="88.33"/><line class="sg" x1="108" y1="108" x2="34.59" y2="88.33"/><line class="sg" x1="108" y1="108" x2="181.41" y2="88.33"/><line class="sg" x1="108" y1="108" x2="108.0" y2="184.0"/><circle class="pt" cx="108" cy="108" r="2.6"/><text class="it" x="102" y="123" text-anchor="end">O</text><circle class="pt" cx="34.59" cy="88.33" r="3.4"/><text class="it" x="25.9" y="90.0" text-anchor="end">M</text><circle class="pt" cx="181.41" cy="88.33" r="3.4"/><text class="it" x="190.1" y="90.0" text-anchor="start">N</text><circle class="pt" cx="108.0" cy="184.0" r="3.4"/><text class="it" x="108.0" y="205.0" text-anchor="middle">F</text></svg>

reasons: used the base angle itself as the central angle
doubled the base angle, as if it were an inscribed angle
used 180 - base as the central angle, forgetting the second base angle

module1.stem: The mean score of 18 players in a basketball game was 13 points. If the highest individual score is removed, the mean score of the remaining 17 players becomes 12.5 points. What was the highest score?
module1.rationale: The 18 values total 234 and the 17 that remain total 212.5, a difference of 21.5.
reasons: reported how far the mean fell, not the value that was taken away
multiplied the fall in the mean by one less than the original count
added the two means

module1.stem:
7x + 2y = 40
63x + 18y = 360

divided r by the multiplier between the two equations and used the two right-hand sides as the shifts
solved the equation for x but wrote that expression as the y-coordinate

Which of the following expressions is equivalent to f(z)/g(z), for z > 11 ?
module1.rationale: z³ − 121z is z(z − 11)(z + 11) and z² − 3z − 88 is (z − 11)(z + 8), so only z − 11 cancels.
reasons: cancelled everything in the numerator against the denominator
cancelled the z in front as well as the shared bracket
cancelled the wrong bracket and kept the one the denominator shares

module2_lower.stem: For a 2-week period in a town in Nebraska, the lowest recorded temperature was 89 degrees Fahrenheit (°F) and the highest recorded temperature was 104°F. Which inequality is true for any recorded temperature t, in °F, in this town for this 2-week period?

used the largest recorded value as the bottom of the range and the sum of the two as the top

reasons: used the largest recorded value as the bottom of the range and the sum of the two as the top
kept only the largest recorded value and read it as a floor rather than as the top of the range
kept only the smallest recorded value and read it as a cap rather than as the bottom of the range

module2_upper.stem: On a car trip, Rhett and Jessica each drove for part of the trip, and the total distance they drove was less than 300 miles. Rhett drove at an average speed of 65 miles per hour (mph), and Jessica drove at an average speed of 45 mph. Which of the following inequalities represents this situation, where x is the number of hours Rhett drove and y is the number of hours Jessica drove?
module2_upper.rationale: Rhett covers 65 miles in each of the x hours, which is 65x, and Jessica covers 45 miles in each of the y hours, which is 45y; the distance altogether is less than 300, so 65x + 45y < 300.
reasons: gave each driver the other driver's average speed and read the limit as a minimum instead of a maximum
read the limit as a minimum instead of a maximum
gave each driver the other driver's average speed

module2_upper.stem: Which of the following is equivalent to w² + 16w + 1?
module2_upper.rationale: Half of 16 is 8, and (w + 8)² already carries 64, so −63 is what is left to reach 1.
reasons: halved the middle coefficient with the wrong sign and corrected the wrong way too
added the correction instead of subtracting it
halved the middle coefficient but changed its sign

module2_upper.stem: Points P, Q, and W lie on a circle. Minor arc PQ has a length of 27 meters and major arc PWQ has a length of 54 meters. What is the circumference, in meters, of the circle?
module2_upper.figure: <svg viewBox="0 0 216 216" width="216" height="216" role="img" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><style>.ax{stroke:currentColor;stroke-width:1.4;fill:none}.gr{stroke:currentColor;stroke-width:.5;opacity:.28}.pt{fill:currentColor}.sg{stroke:currentColor;stroke-width:1.4;fill:none}.lb{fill:currentColor;font:11px ui-sans-serif,system-ui,sans-serif}.it{fill:currentColor;font:italic 13px ui-serif,Georgia,serif}</style><circle class="ax" cx="108" cy="108" r="76"/><circle class="pt" cx="42.18" cy="70.0" r="3.4"/><text class="it" x="34.39" y="69.5" text-anchor="end">P</text><circle class="pt" cx="173.82" cy="70.0" r="3.4"/><text class="it" x="181.61" y="69.5" text-anchor="start">Q</text><circle class="pt" cx="108.0" cy="184.0" r="3.4"/><text class="it" x="108.0" y="205.0" text-anchor="middle">W</text></svg>
module2_upper.rationale: The two arcs make up the whole circle, so the circumference is 27 + 54 = 81.
reasons: gave the minor arc instead of the whole circumference
gave the major arc instead of the whole circumference
doubled the major arc

module2_upper.stem: Which expression is equivalent to (y + z/3)²?
module2_upper.rationale: (y + z/3)² is y² plus twice y·z/3 plus (z/3)², and squaring a fraction squares its denominator too.
reasons: left out the middle term of the square
forgot to double the middle term and squared only the numerator of the fraction
left out the middle term and squared only the numerator of the fraction

module2_upper.stem: In the xy-plane above, points A, B, C, and D lie on the circle with center O. The degree measures of angles AOB and COD are 60° and 10°, respectively. What is the radian measure of angle BOC ?
module2_upper.figure: <svg viewBox="0 0 302 216" width="302" height="216" role="img" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><style>.ax{stroke:currentColor;stroke-width:1.4;fill:none}.gr{stroke:currentColor;stroke-width:.5;opacity:.28}.pt{fill:currentColor}.sg{stroke:currentColor;stroke-width:1.4;fill:none}.lb{fill:currentColor;font:11px ui-sans-serif,system-ui,sans-serif}.it{fill:currentColor;font:italic 13px ui-serif,Georgia,serif}</style><circle class="ax" cx="151" cy="108" r="76"/><line class="sg" x1="151" y1="108" x2="75.0" y2="108.0"/><line class="sg" x1="151" y1="108" x2="227.0" y2="108.0"/><line class="sg" x1="151" y1="108" x2="189.0" y2="42.18"/><line class="sg" x1="151" y1="108" x2="76.15" y2="94.8"/><circle class="pt" cx="151" cy="108" r="2.6"/><text class="it" x="145" y="123" text-anchor="end">O</text><circle class="pt" cx="75.0" cy="108.0" r="3.4"/><text class="it" x="66.0" y="112.0" text-anchor="end">D (−1, 0)</text><circle class="pt" cx="227.0" cy="108.0" r="3.4"/><text class="it" x="236.0" y="112.0" text-anchor="start">A (1, 0)</text><circle class="pt" cx="189.0" cy="42.18" r="3.4"/><text class="it" x="193.5" y="31.39" text-anchor="start">B</text><circle class="pt" cx="76.15" cy="94.8" r="3.4"/><text class="it" x="67.29" y="97.24" text-anchor="end">C</text></svg>
module2_upper.rationale: A, O and D are collinear, so angle BOC is 180 − 60 − 10 = 110 degrees, which is 11π/18 radians.
reasons: added the two marked angles instead of subtracting them from 180
subtracted only one of the two marked angles from 180 degrees
subtracted the marked angles from a full turn instead of a straight angle

module2_upper.stem:
(p³q³r⁶)(p³r⁶ + q⁹r⁻⁸)
Which of the following is equivalent to the expression above?
module2_upper.rationale: p³q³r⁶ multiplies each term inside the parentheses, and the exponents of each variable add.
reasons: kept only the variables that both factors carry, dropping q from the first product and p from the second
left q out of both products because it is missing from one factor of each
multiplied only the first term inside the parentheses by the monomial

module2_upper.stem:
(x + 2)(x + 7) = (x − 2)(x − 7) + 6
Which of the following is a solution to the given equation?
module2_upper.rationale: Both sides carry x², and what is left is 18x = 6, so x = 1/3.
reasons: solved for the wrong sign of x
cancelled both sides entirely and concluded that x is zero
forgot that the x terms appear twice over

module2_upper.stem:
H = 140p + 60
The formula above shows the relationship between Renata's target heart rate H, in beats per minute (bpm), and the intensity level p of different activities. When p = 0, Renata has a resting heart rate. When p = 1, Renata has a maximum heart rate. It is recommended that p be between 0.5 and 0.9 for Renata when training. Which of the following inequalities describes Renata's target training heart rate?
module2_upper.rationale: The smallest the quantity can be is 60 + 140(0.5) = 130, and the largest is 60 + 140(0.9) = 186; the multiplier is positive, so the ends keep their order and 130 ≤ H ≤ 186.
reasons: added the resting heart rate at the top of the range but not at the bottom
multiplied the resting heart rate by each end of the range instead of adding the amount the rate builds up
left the resting heart rate out of both ends of the range

module2_upper.stem:
y = (x)(x − 1)
2x + y = 0
Which ordered pair (x, y) is a solution to the given system of equations?
module2_upper.rationale: Putting the line into y = (x)(x − 1) leaves a quadratic in x whose solutions are −1 and 0, and the line then gives y = 2 and 0.
reasons: named a point on the line that is not on the curve
read the two numbers the brackets give as the coordinates
read the two numbers the brackets give and wrote them the wrong way round

module2_upper.stem: A number x is at most 12 less than 9 times the value of y. If the value of y is −7, what is the greatest possible value of x?
module2_upper.rationale: The condition is x ≤ 9y − 12, and with y = −7 the right side is −75, so the greatest value x can take is −75.

module2_upper.topic_name: One-Variable Data: Distributions and Measures of Centre and Spread
module2_upper.stem:
15, 15, 15, 15, 21, 21, 21, 21, 21, 23, 23, 23, 23, 25, 25
Which frequency table correctly represents the data listed?
module2_upper.rationale: 15 appears 4 times, 21 appears 5 times, 23 appears 4 times, 25 appears 2 times.
reasons: multiplied each value by its count and then swapped the columns
swapped the two columns, reading each count as a data value
multiplied each value by how many times it appears instead of counting the appearances

module2_upper.stem: A shipping service restricts the dimensions of the boxes it will ship for a certain type of service. The restriction states that for boxes shaped like rectangular prisms, the sum of the perimeter of the base of the box and the height of the box cannot exceed 220 inches. The perimeter of the base is determined using the width and length of the box. If a box has a height of 60 inches and its length is 4 times the width, which inequality shows the allowable width x, in inches, of the box?
module2_upper.rationale: The base has perimeter 2(x + 4x) = 10x, so 10x + 60 ≤ 220, leaving x ≤ 16; a width is positive, so 0 < x ≤ 16.
reasons: added the width and the length once each instead of finding the whole perimeter
doubled the length but counted the width only once
used four widths, as though the base were a square

module2_upper.topic_name: One-Variable Data: Distributions and Measures of Centre and Spread
module2_upper.stem: The mean score of 14 players in a basketball game was 54 points. If the highest individual score is removed, the mean score of the remaining 13 players becomes 52.5 points. What was the highest score?
module2_upper.rationale: The 14 values total 756 and the 13 that remain total 682.5, a difference of 73.5.
reasons: reported how far the mean fell, not the value that was taken away
multiplied the fall in the mean by one less than the original count
added the two means

module2_upper.stem: A company selected 140 employees at random from its own employees and randomly assigned them to two groups. One group used a standing desk for 14 weeks and the other used a seated desk. The group that used the standing desk reported significantly greater comfort at work. Which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion from this study?
choices: The standing desk causes an increase in comfort reported at work for all office employees in the country.
There is an association between the standing desk and an increase in comfort reported at work for the 140 employees in the study.
The standing desk causes an increase in comfort reported at work for the employees of this company.
There is an association between the standing desk and an increase in comfort reported at work for all office employees in the country.
latex: The standing desk causes an increase in comfort reported at work for all office employees in the country.
There is an association between the standing desk and an increase in comfort reported at work for the 140 employees in the study.
The standing desk causes an increase in comfort reported at work for the employees of this company.
There is an association between the standing desk and an increase in comfort reported at work for all office employees in the country.
module2_upper.rationale: The employees were randomly assigned, so the difference between the groups is a cause; they were selected at random from the employees of this company, so the conclusion reaches that group.
reasons: generalized past the employees of this company, the group the employees were selected from
under-claimed twice over: random assignment earns a cause, and random selection earns the group the units came from
generalized past the employees of this company, the group the employees were selected from

module2_upper.stem: The line with the equation (3/2)x + (8/5)y = 2 is graphed in the xy-plane. What is the x-coordinate of the x-intercept of the line?
module2_upper.rationale: On the x-axis y is zero, so the term in y drops out and the term in x has to account for the whole right-hand side by itself.

module2_upper.stem: Point O is the center of the circle above, the measure of angle OJK is 65°, and the radius of the circle is 12. What is the length of arc JK ?
module2_upper.figure: <svg viewBox="0 0 216 216" width="216" height="216" role="img" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><style>.ax{stroke:currentColor;stroke-width:1.4;fill:none}.gr{stroke:currentColor;stroke-width:.5;opacity:.28}.pt{fill:currentColor}.sg{stroke:currentColor;stroke-width:1.4;fill:none}.lb{fill:currentColor;font:11px ui-sans-serif,system-ui,sans-serif}.it{fill:currentColor;font:italic 13px ui-serif,Georgia,serif}</style><circle class="ax" cx="108" cy="108" r="76"/><line class="sg" x1="75.88" y1="39.12" x2="140.12" y2="39.12"/><line class="sg" x1="108" y1="108" x2="75.88" y2="39.12"/><line class="sg" x1="108" y1="108" x2="140.12" y2="39.12"/><line class="sg" x1="108" y1="108" x2="108.0" y2="184.0"/><circle class="pt" cx="108" cy="108" r="2.6"/><text class="it" x="102" y="123" text-anchor="end">O</text><circle class="pt" cx="75.88" cy="39.12" r="3.4"/><text class="it" x="72.08" y="27.96" text-anchor="end">J</text><circle class="pt" cx="140.12" cy="39.12" r="3.4"/><text class="it" x="143.92" y="27.96" text-anchor="start">K</text><circle class="pt" cx="108.0" cy="184.0" r="3.4"/><text class="it" x="108.0" y="205.0" text-anchor="middle">G</text></svg>
module2_upper.rationale: OJ and OK are radii, so angle OKJ also measures 65 degrees and the central angle is 180 − 2(65) = 50 degrees. The circumference is 24π, so the arc is (50/360)(24π) = 10π/3.
reasons: used the base angle itself as the central angle
used 180 - base as the central angle, forgetting the second base angle
doubled the base angle, as if it were an inscribed angle

module2_upper.stem: The expression (7n − 18)(11n + 1) is equivalent to the expression an² + bn + c, where a, b, and c are constants. What is the value of b?
module2_upper.rationale: The middle coefficient is the sum of the two cross products, 7 × 1 and −18 × 11.

module2_upper.stem: If √(x⁷)/⁵√(x⁴) = x^(a/b) for all positive values of x, what is the value of a/b ?
module2_upper.rationale: The two radicals are x^(7/2) and x^(4/5), and dividing subtracts the exponents.

module2_upper.stem: One of the factors of 3t³ + 54t² + 135t is t + b, where b is a positive constant. What is the smallest possible value of b?
module2_upper.rationale: 3t³ + 54t² + 135t is 3t(t + 3)(t + 15), so b is 3 or 15.

module1.stem:
|x − 9| = 45
What is the negative solution to the given equation?
module1.rationale: The quantity inside the bars is 45 or −45, so x = 54 or x = −36.

module1.stem: Amara bought two containers of buttons. In the first container 30% of the buttons are black, and in the second container 40% of the buttons are black. Together, the containers have at most 300 black buttons. Which inequality shows this relationship, where x is the total number of buttons in the first container and y is the total number of buttons in the second container?
module1.rationale: 30% of the x buttons in the first container are black, which is 0.3x, and 40% of the y in the second are black, which is 0.4y; together those have to be at most 300, so 0.3x + 0.4y ≤ 300.
reasons: divided by the first digit of each percentage instead of multiplying by the decimal it stands for
used the percentages as whole numbers instead of as decimals
attached each percentage to the other container and read the limit as a minimum instead of a maximum

module1.stem: In the triangle above, a = 91. What is the value of b ?
