reasons: stopped at 2b rather than dividing by 2
subtracted the marked angle from 90 degrees
added the two known measures instead of subtracting them from 180 degrees

module1.stem: A market researcher selected 150 people at random from a group of people who indicated that they liked a certain book. The 150 people were shown a movie based on the book and then asked whether they liked or disliked the movie. Of those surveyed, 80% said they liked the movie. Which of the following inferences can appropriately be drawn from this survey result?
choices: Most people who like this book will like this movie.
At least 80% of people who go see movies will like this movie.
Most people who like this book will dislike this movie.
Most people who dislike this book will dislike this movie.
latex: Most people who like this book will like this movie.
At least 80% of people who go see movies will like this movie.
Most people who like this book will dislike this movie.
Most people who dislike this book will dislike this movie.
module1.rationale: The people were selected at random from people who like this book, so only a claim about that group is licensed; 80% of one sample estimates the population rather than fixing it, so only “most” is supported.
reasons: generalized past the sampling frame, and repeated the sample's percentage as if it held exactly
read the minority response of the sample as its majority response
swapped the group the sample came from for its complement, and the response with it

module1.stem: Which of the following is an equivalent form of 3y⁷ − 3y⁶ + 15y ?
module1.rationale: Every term holds at least one y and a factor of 3, so 3y comes out and each exponent drops by one.
reasons: took the common factor out but reduced none of the exponents
attached the powers of the variable to the coefficient instead of to the variable
took only the variable out and subtracted one from every coefficient instead of dividing by the common factor

module1.stem:
5x² + 15x + 8 = 0
How many distinct real solutions are there to the given equation?
module1.rationale: The equation has a discriminant of 65, so it has exactly two real solutions.
reasons: counted the two square roots of a positive number as a single solution
read the sign of the discriminant the wrong way round, and concluded that the curve never meets the axis
read the equation as an identity, true for every value of x

module1.stem: For a 6-week period in a town in Vermont, the lowest recorded temperature was 87 degrees Fahrenheit (°F) and the highest recorded temperature was 128°F. Which inequality is true for any recorded temperature t, in °F, in this town for this 6-week period?
module1.rationale: Every recorded value is at least the smallest, 87, and at most the largest, 128; both were recorded, so both ends belong to the range and 87 ≤ t ≤ 128.
reasons: kept only the smallest recorded value and read it as a cap rather than as the bottom of the range
used the largest recorded value as the bottom of the range and the sum of the two as the top
kept only the largest recorded value and read it as a floor rather than as the top of the range

module1.stem: A certain elephant weighs 210 pounds at birth and gains more than 3 but less than 4 pounds per day during its first year. Which of the following inequalities represents all possible weights w, in pounds, for the elephant 85 days after birth?
module1.rationale: The smallest the quantity can be is 210 + 85(3) = 465, and the largest is 210 + 85(4) = 550; the multiplier is positive, so the ends keep their order and 465 < w < 550.
reasons: multiplied the birth weight by each end of the range instead of adding the amount the rate builds up
added the birth weight at the top of the range but not at the bottom
left the birth weight out of both ends of the range

module1.stem: Points B, C, and W lie on a circle. Minor arc BC has a length of 5 feet and major arc BWC has a length of 10 feet. What is the circumference, in feet, of the circle?
module1.figure: <svg viewBox="0 0 216 216" width="216" height="216" role="img" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><style>.ax{stroke:currentColor;stroke-width:1.4;fill:none}.gr{stroke:currentColor;stroke-width:.5;opacity:.28}.pt{fill:currentColor}.sg{stroke:currentColor;stroke-width:1.4;fill:none}.lb{fill:currentColor;font:11px ui-sans-serif,system-ui,sans-serif}.it{fill:currentColor;font:italic 13px ui-serif,Georgia,serif}</style><circle class="ax" cx="108" cy="108" r="76"/><circle class="pt" cx="42.18" cy="70.0" r="3.4"/><text class="it" x="34.39" y="69.5" text-anchor="end">B</text><circle class="pt" cx="173.82" cy="70.0" r="3.4"/><text class="it" x="181.61" y="69.5" text-anchor="start">C</text><circle class="pt" cx="108.0" cy="184.0" r="3.4"/><text class="it" x="108.0" y="205.0" text-anchor="middle">W</text></svg>
module1.rationale: The two arcs make up the whole circle, so the circumference is 5 + 10 = 15.

module1.topic_name: One-Variable Data: Distributions and Measures of Centre and Spread
module1.stem:
4, 19, 13, 5
The mean of the list of numbers above is what fraction of the sum of the four numbers?
module1.rationale: The mean is the sum divided by 4, so it is one fourth of the sum whatever the numbers are.

module1.stem: The sum of −4j² − 3j − 24 and −4j² − j + 38 can be written in the form aj² + bj + c, where a, b, and c are constants. What is the value of a + b + c ?
module1.rationale: Adding like terms gives −8j² − 4j + 14, and a, b and c are its three coefficients.

module1.stem: A model estimates that whales from the genus Balaenoptera travel 72 to 78 miles in the ocean each day during their migration. Based on this model, which inequality represents the estimated total number of miles, x, one of these whales could travel in 11 days of its migration?
module1.rationale: Each of the 11 days adds between 72 and 78 miles, so the smallest total is (72)(11) and the largest is (78)(11); multiplying by a positive number keeps the two ends in order, so (72)(11) ≤ x ≤ (78)(11).
reasons: added the two quantities instead of multiplying them
divided by the quantity that should have been multiplied, which also turns the two ends round
subtracted the two quantities instead of multiplying them

module1.stem: A cargo helicopter delivers only 70-pound packages and 180-pound packages. For each delivery trip, the cargo helicopter must carry at least 16 packages, and the total weight of the packages can be at most 2,300 pounds. What is the maximum number of 180-pound packages that the cargo helicopter can carry per trip?
module1.rationale: Carrying 16 of the lighter packages weighs 1,120 pounds, and each swap to a heavier one adds 110 pounds. The cap leaves 1,180 pounds to spend on swaps, so at most 10 of the packages can be the heavier kind.
reasons: stopped one swap short of the weight the load allows
rounded the number of swaps up instead of down
divided the whole weight allowance by the heavier package and ignored the smallest number of packages

module1.stem: Which expression is equivalent to (s + t/3)²?
module1.rationale: (s + t/3)² is s² plus twice s·t/3 plus (t/3)², and squaring a fraction squares its denominator too.
reasons: forgot to double the middle term and squared only the numerator of the fraction
left out the middle term of the square
left out the middle term and squared only the numerator of the fraction

module1.stem: A moving truck can tow a trailer if the combined weight of the trailer and the boxes it contains is no more than 4,100 pounds. What is the maximum number of boxes this truck can tow in a trailer with a weight of 250 pounds if each box weighs 40 pounds?
module1.rationale: The condition is 250 + 40n ≤ 4,100. With n = 96 the combined weight is 4,090, which meets it, and with n = 97 it is 4,130, which does not, so the greatest whole number that works is 96.
reasons: rounded the quotient up instead of down
left the fixed charge out of the total
left the fixed charge out and rounded up

module1.topic_name: One-Variable Data: Distributions and Measures of Centre and Spread
module1.stem:
20, 20, 20, 20, 20, 21, 21, 21, 36, 36, 36, 36, 36
Which frequency table correctly represents the data listed?
module1.rationale: 20 appears 5 times, 21 appears 3 times, 36 appears 5 times.
reasons: multiplied each value by its count and then swapped the columns
multiplied each value by how many times it appears instead of counting the appearances
swapped the two columns, reading each count as a data value

module1.stem: If √(t¹¹)/³√(t⁴) = t^(a/b) for all positive values of t, what is the value of a/b ?
module1.rationale: The two radicals are t^(11/2) and t^(4/3), and dividing subtracts the exponents.

module1.stem: A number x is at most 10 less than 5 times the value of y. If the value of y is −7, what is the greatest possible value of x?
module1.rationale: The condition is x ≤ 5y − 10, and with y = −7 the right side is −45, so the greatest value x can take is −45.

module1.stem: A square and a circle have the same area. If the area of the circle is 625π, what is the side length of the square?
module1.rationale: The circle has area pi(25)^2 = 625π; a square of that area has side 25√π.
reasons: found the area as πr, forgetting to square the radius, and then took the square root
used the radius as the side length
used πr, forgetting to square the radius or take the root

module1.topic_name: One-Variable Data: Distributions and Measures of Centre and Spread
module1.stem: The mean height of the 20 trees in an orchard is 56.5 feet. After the tallest tree is cut down, the mean height of the remaining 19 trees is 55.25 feet. What was the height, in feet, of the tree that was cut down?
module1.rationale: The 20 values total 1,130 and the 19 that remain total 1,049.75, a difference of 80.25.
reasons: reported how far the mean fell, not the value that was taken away
multiplied the fall in the mean by one less than the original count
added the two means

module1.stem: A psychologist set up an experiment to study the tendency of a person to select the first item when presented with a series of items. In the experiment, 180 people were presented with a set of four pictures arranged in random order. Each person was asked to choose the most appealing picture. Of the first 90 participants, 59 chose the first picture in the set. Among the remaining 90 participants, p people chose the first picture in the set. If more than 25% of all participants chose the first picture in the set, which of the following inequalities best describes the possible values of p ?
module1.rationale: Altogether p + 59 people chose the first picture, and that has to be more than 25% of the 180 participants; only 90 people are left to choose, so p + 59 > 0.25(180), where p ≤ 90.
reasons: subtracted the first group's count instead of adding it
added the first group's count to the total number of participants instead of to the unknown
subtracted the first group's count from the total number of participants instead of adding it to the unknown

module1.stem: The equation (x² + 3x − 10)/(x + 5) = px + k is true for all x ≠ −5, where p and k are integers. What is the value of p + k ?
module1.rationale: x² + 3x − 10 is (x + 5)(x − 2), so dividing by x + 5 leaves x − 2.
reasons: took k from the divisor rather than from the quotient
reported k on its own
reported p on its own

module2_lower.stem: For a 3-week period in a town in Illinois, the lowest recorded temperature was 30 degrees Fahrenheit (°F) and the highest recorded temperature was 54°F. Which inequality is true for any recorded temperature t, in °F, in this town for this 3-week period?
module2_lower.rationale: Every recorded value is at least the smallest, 30, and at most the largest, 54; both were recorded, so both ends belong to the range and 30 ≤ t ≤ 54.
reasons: kept only the smallest recorded value and read it as a cap rather than as the bottom of the range
kept only the largest recorded value and read it as a floor rather than as the top of the range
used the largest recorded value as the bottom of the range and the sum of the two as the top

module2_lower.topic_name: One-Variable Data: Distributions and Measures of Centre and Spread
module2_lower.stem: Each volunteer in a cleanup project was asked to choose a small gift labeled A, B, C, or D. The bar graph shows the number of volunteers who chose each gift. How many more volunteers chose gift B than gift D?

module2_lower.rationale: Gift B shows 67 and gift D shows 62, and 67 − 62 = 5.
reasons: read the shorter bar, gift D, instead of the difference
read the taller bar, gift B, instead of the difference
added the two bars instead of subtracting

module2_lower.stem: A geologist estimates that the volume of a slab of marble is greater than 20.5 cubic feet but less than 22.4 cubic feet. The geologist also estimates that the slab of marble weighs 265 pounds per cubic foot of volume. Which inequality represents this situation, where x represents the estimated total weight, in pounds, of the slab of marble?
module2_lower.rationale: Each cubic foot weighs 265 pounds, so the smallest total is 265(20.5) and the largest is 265(22.4); multiplying by a positive number keeps the two ends in order, so 265(20.5) < x < 265(22.4).
reasons: subtracted the two quantities instead of multiplying them
divided by the quantity that should have been multiplied, which also turns the two ends round
added the two quantities instead of multiplying them

module2_lower.topic_name: One-Variable Data: Distributions and Measures of Centre and Spread
module2_lower.stem:
68, 70, 86, 59, 69
What is the median of the data shown?
module2_lower.rationale: In order the values are 59, 68, 69, 70, 86, so the middle of the 5 values is 69.
reasons: found the range instead of the median
read the least value instead of the middle one
read the greatest value instead of the middle one

module2_lower.stem: A clothing store is having a sale on ties and jackets. During the sale, the cost of each tie is $25 and the cost of each jacket is $5. Priya can spend greater than $500 at the store. If Priya buys x ties and y jackets, which of the following must be true?
module2_lower.rationale: x ties at $25 each cost 25x, and y jackets at $5 each cost 5y; the two together have to come to greater than $500, so 25x + 5y > 500.
reasons: attached each price to the other kind of item
attached each price to the other kind of item and read the limit as a maximum instead of a minimum
read the limit as a maximum instead of a minimum

module2_lower.stem: The table above summarizes the responses of 1,200 residents to a survey. Based on the table, how many of those surveyed travel to the city center by either bicycle or some other means?
reasons: gave the percentage rather than the number of people it stands for
multiplied the two percentages instead of adding them
used the Bicycle row alone

module2_lower.stem: The point (6, 9) in the xy-plane is a solution to which of the following systems of inequalities?
module2_lower.rationale: The first coordinate, 6, is positive and the second, 9, is positive, so the point lies where x > 0, y > 0.
reasons: read the second coordinate as negative, although 9 is positive
read the first coordinate as negative, although 6 is positive
read both coordinates as having the opposite sign

module2_lower.stem: What is the value of sin 145π/3 ?
module2_lower.rationale: 145π/3 and π/3 differ by whole turns, so sin 145π/3 = sin π/3 = √3/2.
reasons: gave the cosine of the angle instead
used the 45-degree reference value
dropped the 2 in the denominator of the reference value

module2_lower.stem:
|x − 11| = 15
What is the negative solution to the given equation?
module2_lower.rationale: The quantity inside the bars is 15 or −15, so x = 26 or x = −4.

module2_lower.stem: Which of the following is equivalent to the expression 5r⁹ − 5r⁸ + 10r ?
module2_lower.rationale: Every term holds at least one r and a factor of 5, so 5r comes out and each exponent drops by one.
reasons: took only the variable out and subtracted one from every coefficient instead of dividing by the common factor
attached the powers of the variable to the coefficient instead of to the variable
took the common factor out but reduced none of the exponents

module2_lower.stem:
4x² − 12x + 3 = 0
How many distinct real solutions are there to the given equation?
module2_lower.rationale: The equation has a discriminant of 96, so it has exactly two real solutions.
reasons: counted the two square roots of a positive number as a single solution
read the sign of the discriminant the wrong way round, and concluded that the curve never meets the axis
read the equation as an identity, true for every value of x

module2_lower.stem: The sum of −w² − 7w + 25 and 5w² − 3w + 16 can be written in the form aw² + bw + c, where a, b, and c are constants. What is the value of a + b + c ?
module2_lower.rationale: Adding like terms gives 4w² − 10w + 41, and a, b and c are its three coefficients.

module2_lower.stem: In the xy-plane, a circle with a radius of 9 has center (−11, 2). Which of the following is an equation of the circle?
module2_lower.rationale: A circle with center (h, k) and radius r has equation (x − h)² + (y − k)² = r², which gives (x + 11)² + (y − 2)² = 81.
reasons: used the radius itself instead of its square
kept the signs of the center and used the radius instead of its square
kept the signs of the center's coordinates instead of changing them

module2_lower.stem: Which of the following is equivalent to a² + 10a + 9 ?
module2_lower.rationale: Half of 10 is 5, and (a + 5)² already carries 25, so −16 is what is left to reach 9.
reasons: halved the middle coefficient but changed its sign
halved the middle coefficient with the wrong sign and corrected the wrong way too
added the correction instead of subtracting it

module2_lower.stem: Points P, Q, R, and T lie on the circle shown, which has center O. The degree measures of angles POQ and ROT are 55° and 25°, respectively. What is the radian measure of angle QOR ?

reasons: added the two marked angles instead of subtracting them from 180
subtracted only one of the two marked angles from 180 degrees
subtracted the marked angles from a full turn instead of a straight angle

module2_lower.stem: Which expression is equivalent to (u⁻⁵v³w³)(u²w⁷ + v⁶w⁻⁵) ?
module2_lower.rationale: u⁻⁵v³w³ multiplies each term inside the parentheses, and the exponents of each variable add.
reasons: multiplied only the first term inside the parentheses by the monomial
kept only the variables that both factors carry, dropping v from the first product and u from the second
left v out of both products because it is missing from one factor of each

module2_lower.stem:
(2k + 8)² − (k − 8) + 5(k + 6)
Which of the following is equivalent to the expression above?
module2_lower.rationale: (2k + 8)² is 4k² + 32k + 64, and the minus sign in front of the second bracket reaches its constant too.
reasons: left out the middle term of the square and did not change the sign of the subtracted constant
did not change the sign of the constant in the bracket that is subtracted
left out the middle term of the square

module2_lower.stem: An event planner is planning a party. It costs the event planner a onetime fee of $105 to rent the venue and $40 per attendee. The event planner has a budget of $530. What is the greatest number of attendees possible without exceeding the budget?
module2_lower.rationale: The condition is 105 + 40n ≤ 530. With n = 10 the cost is $505.00, which meets it, and with n = 11 it is $545.00, which does not, so the greatest whole number that works is 10.

module2_lower.stem:
(x + 2)(x + 3) = (x − 2)(x − 3) − 20
Which of the following is a solution to the given equation?
module2_lower.rationale: Both sides carry x², and what is left is 10x = −20, so x = −2.
reasons: added the two bracket numbers and changed the sign
read the second bracket's number as the solution
cancelled both sides entirely and concluded that x is zero

module2_lower.stem: Point O is the center of the circle above, the measure of angle OBC is 15°, and the radius of the circle is 40. What is the measure, in degrees, of angle BOC?
module2_lower.figure: <svg viewBox="0 0 216 216" width="216" height="216" role="img" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><style>.ax{stroke:currentColor;stroke-width:1.4;fill:none}.gr{stroke:currentColor;stroke-width:.5;opacity:.28}.pt{fill:currentColor}.sg{stroke:currentColor;stroke-width:1.4;fill:none}.lb{fill:currentColor;font:11px ui-sans-serif,system-ui,sans-serif}.it{fill:currentColor;font:italic 13px ui-serif,Georgia,serif}</style><circle class="ax" cx="108" cy="108" r="76"/><line class="sg" x1="34.59" y1="88.33" x2="181.41" y2="88.33"/><line class="sg" x1="108" y1="108" x2="34.59" y2="88.33"/><line class="sg" x1="108" y1="108" x2="181.41" y2="88.33"/><line class="sg" x1="108" y1="108" x2="108.0" y2="184.0"/><circle class="pt" cx="108" cy="108" r="2.6"/><text class="it" x="102" y="123" text-anchor="end">O</text><circle class="pt" cx="34.59" cy="88.33" r="3.4"/><text class="it" x="25.9" y="90.0" text-anchor="end">B</text><circle class="pt" cx="181.41" cy="88.33" r="3.4"/><text class="it" x="190.1" y="90.0" text-anchor="start">C</text><circle class="pt" cx="108.0" cy="184.0" r="3.4"/><text class="it" x="108.0" y="205.0" text-anchor="middle">E</text></svg>
module2_lower.rationale: OB and OC are radii, so the triangle is isosceles and angle OCB also measures 15 degrees. That leaves 180 − 2(15) = 150 degrees at the center.

module2_lower.stem: A number x is at least 4 less than 9 times the value of y. If the value of y is 9, what is the least possible value of x?
module2_lower.rationale: The condition is x ≥ 9y − 4, and with y = 9 the right side is 77, so the least value x can take is 77.

module2_lower.stem: A psychologist set up an experiment to study the tendency of a person to select the first item when presented with a series of items. In the experiment, 300 people were presented with a set of five pictures arranged in random order. Each person was asked to choose the most appealing picture. Of the first 150 participants, 45 chose the first picture in the set. Among the remaining 150 participants, p people chose the first picture in the set. If more than 15% of all participants chose the first picture in the set, which of the following inequalities best describes the possible values of p ?
module2_lower.rationale: Altogether p + 45 people chose the first picture, and that has to be more than 15% of the 300 participants; only 150 people are left to choose, so p + 45 > 0.15(300), where p ≤ 150.
reasons: added the first group's count to the total number of participants instead of to the unknown
subtracted the first group's count instead of adding it
subtracted the first group's count from the total number of participants instead of adding it to the unknown

module2_upper.stem: What is the value of sin 517π/3, where the angle is measured in radians?
module2_upper.rationale: 517π/3 and π/3 differ by whole turns, so sin 517π/3 = sin π/3 = √3/2.
reasons: gave the cosine of the angle instead
used the 45-degree reference value
dropped the 2 in the denominator of the reference value

module2_upper.stem: A geologist estimates that the volume of a slab of granite is greater than 7.7 cubic feet but less than 10.3 cubic feet. The geologist also estimates that the slab of granite weighs 110 pounds per cubic foot of volume. Which inequality represents this situation, where x represents the estimated total weight, in pounds, of the slab of granite?
module2_upper.rationale: Each cubic foot weighs 110 pounds, so the smallest total is 110(7.7) and the largest is 110(10.3); multiplying by a positive number keeps the two ends in order, so 110(7.7) < x < 110(10.3).
reasons: divided by the quantity that should have been multiplied, which also turns the two ends round
added the two quantities instead of multiplying them
subtracted the two quantities instead of multiplying them

module2_upper.stem: During spring migration, a monarch butterfly traveled a minimum of 78 miles and a maximum of 107 miles between stopover locations. Which inequality represents this situation, where d is a possible distance, in miles, this monarch butterfly traveled between stopover locations during spring migration?
module2_upper.rationale: Every recorded value is at least the smallest, 78, and at most the largest, 107; both were recorded, so both ends belong to the range and 78 ≤ d ≤ 107.
reasons: kept only the largest recorded value and read it as a floor rather than as the top of the range
used the largest recorded value as the bottom of the range and the sum of the two as the top
kept only the smallest recorded value and read it as a cap rather than as the bottom of the range

module2_upper.stem: The sum of 4w² − w − 17 and −3w² + 9w + 18 can be written in the form aw² + bw + c, where a, b, and c are constants. What is the value of a + b + c ?
module2_upper.rationale: Adding like terms gives w² + 8w + 1, and a, b and c are its three coefficients.

module2_upper.stem: Points B, C, and Q lie on the circle shown. On this circle, minor arc BC has a length of 50 meters and major arc BQC has a length of 350 meters. What is the circumference, in meters, of the circle shown?
module2_upper.figure: <svg viewBox="0 0 216 216" width="216" height="216" role="img" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><style>.ax{stroke:currentColor;stroke-width:1.4;fill:none}.gr{stroke:currentColor;stroke-width:.5;opacity:.28}.pt{fill:currentColor}.sg{stroke:currentColor;stroke-width:1.4;fill:none}.lb{fill:currentColor;font:11px ui-sans-serif,system-ui,sans-serif}.it{fill:currentColor;font:italic 13px ui-serif,Georgia,serif}</style><circle class="ax" cx="108" cy="108" r="76"/><circle class="pt" cx="78.92" cy="37.79" r="3.4"/><text class="it" x="75.47" y="26.47" text-anchor="end">B</text><circle class="pt" cx="137.08" cy="37.79" r="3.4"/><text class="it" x="140.53" y="26.47" text-anchor="start">C</text><circle class="pt" cx="108.0" cy="184.0" r="3.4"/><text class="it" x="108.0" y="205.0" text-anchor="middle">Q</text></svg>
module2_upper.rationale: The two arcs make up the whole circle, so the circumference is 50 + 350 = 400.
reasons: gave the minor arc instead of the whole circumference
subtracted the two arcs instead of adding them
gave the major arc instead of the whole circumference

module2_upper.stem: Which of the following is an equivalent form of t² + 14t + 17 ?
module2_upper.rationale: Half of 14 is 7, and (t + 7)² already carries 49, so −32 is what is left to reach 17.
reasons: halved the middle coefficient but changed its sign
added the correction instead of subtracting it
halved the middle coefficient with the wrong sign and corrected the wrong way too

module2_upper.stem: In the xy-plane above, points A, B, C, and D lie on the circle with center O. The degree measures of angles AOB and COD are 60° and 50°, respectively. What is the radian measure of angle BOC ?
module2_upper.figure: <svg viewBox="0 0 302 216" width="302" height="216" role="img" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><style>.ax{stroke:currentColor;stroke-width:1.4;fill:none}.gr{stroke:currentColor;stroke-width:.5;opacity:.28}.pt{fill:currentColor}.sg{stroke:currentColor;stroke-width:1.4;fill:none}.lb{fill:currentColor;font:11px ui-sans-serif,system-ui,sans-serif}.it{fill:currentColor;font:italic 13px ui-serif,Georgia,serif}</style><circle class="ax" cx="151" cy="108" r="76"/><line class="sg" x1="151" y1="108" x2="75.0" y2="108.0"/><line class="sg" x1="151" y1="108" x2="227.0" y2="108.0"/><line class="sg" x1="151" y1="108" x2="189.0" y2="42.18"/><line class="sg" x1="151" y1="108" x2="102.15" y2="49.78"/><circle class="pt" cx="151" cy="108" r="2.6"/><text class="it" x="145" y="123" text-anchor="end">O</text><circle class="pt" cx="75.0" cy="108.0" r="3.4"/><text class="it" x="66.0" y="112.0" text-anchor="end">D (−1, 0)</text><circle class="pt" cx="227.0" cy="108.0" r="3.4"/><text class="it" x="236.0" y="112.0" text-anchor="start">A (1, 0)</text><circle class="pt" cx="189.0" cy="42.18" r="3.4"/><text class="it" x="193.5" y="31.39" text-anchor="start">B</text><circle class="pt" cx="102.15" cy="49.78" r="3.4"/><text class="it" x="96.36" y="39.89" text-anchor="end">C</text></svg>
module2_upper.rationale: A, O and D are collinear, so angle BOC is 180 − 60 − 50 = 70 degrees, which is 7π/18 radians.
reasons: added the two marked angles instead of subtracting them from 180
subtracted only one of the two marked angles from 180 degrees
subtracted the marked angles from a full turn instead of a straight angle

module2_upper.stem:
³√(a³b¹²)
Which of the following expressions is equivalent to the expression above?
module2_upper.rationale: A root of index 3 divides each exponent by 3, so a³ becomes a and b¹² becomes b⁴.
reasons: treated a³ under a root of index 3 as 1
subtracted the index from the exponents instead of dividing by it
subtracted the index from the exponents instead of dividing by it, and dropped a

module2_upper.stem: Which of the following expressions is equivalent to (p − 7q)(5p − 4q) − 14q(−2p + 2q) ?
module2_upper.rationale: The two brackets multiply term by term, and −14q then multiplies both terms of (−2p + 2q).
reasons: multiplied the first brackets out but kept the sign of the last term of the second product
added the terms instead of multiplying the brackets out
used the minus sign in front of the second product twice -- once inside it and once again when combining

module2_upper.stem: The average annual energy cost for a certain home is $3,980. The homeowner plans to spend $21,000 to install a geothermal heating system. The homeowner estimates that the average annual energy cost will then be $2,284. Which of the following inequalities can be solved to find t, the number of years after installation at which the total amount of energy cost savings will exceed the installation cost?
module2_upper.rationale: Each year saves 3,980 − 2,284 dollars, so t years save (3,980 − 2,284)t, and that has to pass the $21,000 it cost to install, so 21,000 < (3,980 − 2,284)t.
reasons: compared the two the wrong way round, so the saving never catches the installation cost up
divided the two annual costs instead of subtracting them
subtracted one year's old cost from the installation cost instead of finding the yearly saving

module2_upper.stem: Which of the following is an equivalent form of √(9u⁶v⁶)/u² ?
module2_upper.rationale: √(9u⁶v⁶) is 3u³v³, and dividing by u² subtracts 2 from the exponent of u.
reasons: halved the coefficient instead of taking its square root, and never divided by u²
used the square root of the coefficient as the root's index and divided each exponent by it
subtracted the exponents the wrong way round and dropped the minus sign

module2_upper.stem: A number x is at least 3 more than 5 times the value of y. If the value of y is −8, what is the least possible value of x?
module2_upper.rationale: The condition is x ≥ 5y + 3, and with y = −8 the right side is −37, so the least value x can take is −37.

module2_upper.stem: An agronomist selected 40 plots at random from the plots on a farm and randomly assigned them to two groups. One group was given a new fertilizer for 7 weeks and the other was given the usual one. The group given the new fertilizer had a significantly higher yield. Which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion from this study?
choices: The new fertilizer causes an increase in yield for all the plots in the region.
The new fertilizer causes an increase in yield for the plots on this farm.
The new fertilizer causes an increase in yield for the 40 plots in the study.
There is an association between the new fertilizer and an increase in yield for all the plots in the region.
latex: The new fertilizer causes an increase in yield for all the plots in the region.
The new fertilizer causes an increase in yield for the plots on this farm.
The new fertilizer causes an increase in yield for the 40 plots in the study.
There is an association between the new fertilizer and an increase in yield for all the plots in the region.
module2_upper.rationale: The plots were randomly assigned, so the difference between the groups is a cause; they were selected at random from the plots on this farm, so the conclusion reaches that group.
reasons: generalized past the plots on this farm, the group the plots were selected from
kept the conclusion inside the study although the units were selected at random from a whole group
generalized past the plots on this farm, the group the plots were selected from

module2_upper.stem:
6x + 2y = 29
54x + 18y = 261
For each real number r, which of the following points lies on the graph of each equation in the xy-plane for the given system?
module2_upper.rationale: The second equation is the first multiplied by 9, so the two draw the same line and any point on it will do. Letting y be r and solving 6x + 2y = 29 for x gives every such point at once.
reasons: solved the equation for x but wrote that expression as the y-coordinate
divided r by the multiplier between the two equations and used the two right-hand sides as the shifts
solved for y but kept the sign of the x term, which changes the line

module2_upper.stem: The mean amount of time that the 12 employees of a construction company have worked for the company is 18.5 years. After one of the employees leaves the company, the mean amount of time that the remaining employees have worked for the company is reduced to 18.25 years. How many years did the employee who left the company work for the company?
module2_upper.rationale: The 12 values total 222 and the 11 that remain total 200.75, a difference of 21.25.
reasons: reported how far the mean fell, not the value that was taken away
multiplied the fall in the mean by one less than the original count
added the two means

module2_upper.stem: Devon is working this summer as part of a crew on a farm, and earned $10 per hour for the first 15 hours worked this week. Because of that performance, the crew leader raised the salary to $12 per hour for the rest of the week. Devon saves 90% of the earnings from each week. What is the least number of hours Devon must work the rest of the week to save at least $210 for the week?
module2_upper.rationale: The condition is 0.9(150 + 12n) ≥ 210. With n = 7 the savings is $210.60, which meets it, and with n = 6 it is $199.80, which does not, so the least whole number that works is 7.
reasons: multiplied the target by the savings fraction instead of dividing by it
applied the savings fraction twice, once to the target and once to the hourly pay
used the first block's hourly rate for the whole week and left out the money already earned

module2_upper.stem: A circle has a radius of 19. What is the perimeter of a square whose area is equal to the area of this circle?
module2_upper.rationale: The circle has area pi(19)^2 = 361π; a square of that area has side 19√π, so its perimeter is 76√π.
reasons: found the area as πr, forgetting to square the radius, and then took the square root
used the radius as the side length
used πr, forgetting to square the radius or take the root

module2_upper.stem: One of the factors of 4w³ + 100w² + 600w is w + b, where b is a positive constant. What is the smallest possible value of b?

2x² − 2x + c = 0
In the given equation, c is a constant. The equation has exactly one solution. What is the value of c?
module2_upper.rationale: One solution means the discriminant is zero, so 4 − 8c = 0 and c = 0.5.

module2_upper.stem: The graph of the function f, defined by f(x) = (−1/2)(x − 7)² + 8, is shown in the xy-plane above. If the function g (not shown) is defined by g(x) = −x + 3, what is one possible value of a such that f(a) = g(a) ?
module2_upper.rationale: Setting (−1/2)(x − 7)² + 8 equal to −x + 3 and gathering gives −(1/2)a² + 8a − 39/2 = 0, so a = 3 or a = 13.

module1.stem:
|x + 4| = 12
What is the positive solution to the given equation?
module1.rationale: The quantity inside the bars is 12 or −12, so x = 8 or x = −16.

module1.stem: During spring migration, a sandhill crane traveled a minimum of 26 miles and a maximum of 67 miles between stopover locations. Which inequality represents this situation, where d is a possible distance, in miles, this sandhill crane traveled between stopover locations during spring migration?
module1.rationale: Every recorded value is at least the smallest, 26, and at most the largest, 67; both were recorded, so both ends belong to the range and 26 ≤ d ≤ 67.
reasons: kept only the largest recorded value and read it as a floor rather than as the top of the range
kept only the smallest recorded value and read it as a cap rather than as the bottom of the range
used the largest recorded value as the bottom of the range and the sum of the two as the top

module1.stem: Which of the following is equivalent to 8d² + 40 ?
module1.rationale: 8 is the largest number that divides both 8 and 40, and each term inside the parentheses is what is left after dividing by it.
reasons: added the common factor to the constant instead of dividing by it
took the common factor out but left the constant term undivided
subtracted the common factor from the constant instead of dividing by it

module1.stem:
−2x² − 16x − 9 = 0
How many distinct real solutions are there to the given equation?
module1.rationale: The equation has a discriminant of 184, so it has exactly two real solutions.
reasons: read the equation as an identity, true for every value of x
counted the two square roots of a positive number as a single solution
read the sign of the discriminant the wrong way round, and concluded that the curve never meets the axis

module1.stem: Normal body temperature for an adult is between 97°F and 99.4°F, inclusive. If Noor, an adult, has a body temperature that is considered to be normal, which of the following could be that body temperature?
module1.rationale: A normal body temperature is anywhere from 97°F to 99.4°F, and 97.1°F is the only one of the four printed values in that range.
reasons: below the lower end of the range, 97°F, by more than a degree
just below the lower end of the range, 97°F, which a normal reading has to reach
above the upper end of the range, 99.4°F, which a normal reading cannot pass

module1.stem:
H = 140p + 55
The formula above shows the relationship between Renata's target heart rate H, in beats per minute (bpm), and the intensity level p of different activities. When p = 0, Renata has a resting heart rate. When p = 1, Renata has a maximum heart rate. It is recommended that p be between 0.35 and 0.6 for Renata when training. Which of the following inequalities describes Renata's target training heart rate?
module1.rationale: The smallest the quantity can be is 55 + 140(0.35) = 104, and the largest is 55 + 140(0.6) = 139; the multiplier is positive, so the ends keep their order and 104 ≤ H ≤ 139.
reasons: left the resting heart rate out of both ends of the range
added the resting heart rate at the bottom of the range but not at the top
added the resting heart rate at the top of the range but not at the bottom

module1.stem:
10, 4, 8, 9, 2, 20, 16, 3, 3, 18
The mean of the list of numbers above is what fraction of the sum of the ten numbers?
module1.rationale: The mean is the sum divided by 10, so it is one tenth of the sum whatever the numbers are.

module1.stem:
(z + 2)((3/2)z + 1/4)
The expression above is equivalent to az² + bz + c, where a, b, and c are constants. What is the value of b?
module1.rationale: The middle coefficient is the sum of the two cross products, 1 × 1/4 and 2 × 3/2.

module1.stem: The average annual energy cost for a certain home is $4,348. The homeowner plans to spend $20,000 to install a geothermal heating system. The homeowner estimates that the average annual energy cost will then be $1,128. Which of the following inequalities can be solved to find t, the number of years after installation at which the total amount of energy cost savings will exceed the installation cost?
module1.rationale: Each year saves 4,348 − 1,128 dollars, so t years save (4,348 − 1,128)t, and that has to pass the $20,000 it cost to install, so 20,000 < (4,348 − 1,128)t.
reasons: divided the two annual costs instead of subtracting them
subtracted one year's old cost from the installation cost instead of finding the yearly saving
compared the two the wrong way round, so the saving never catches the installation cost up

module1.stem: A model estimates that whales from the genus Megaptera travel 58 to 61 miles in the ocean each day during their migration. Based on this model, which inequality represents the estimated total number of miles, x, one of these whales could travel in 33 days of its migration?
module1.rationale: Each of the 33 days adds between 58 and 61 miles, so the smallest total is (58)(33) and the largest is (61)(33); multiplying by a positive number keeps the two ends in order, so (58)(33) ≤ x ≤ (61)(33).
reasons: divided by the quantity that should have been multiplied, which also turns the two ends round
added the two quantities instead of multiplying them
subtracted the two quantities instead of multiplying them

module1.stem: Which of the following is an equivalent form of (3t + 3)² − (6t² + 4) ?
module1.rationale: (3t + 3)² is 9t² + 18t + 9, and every term of the second bracket is then subtracted.
reasons: doubled each term instead of squaring and then added the two constants rather than subtracting
doubled each term instead of squaring the binomial, so the middle term never appeared
subtracted the two constant terms the wrong way round

module1.stem:
y ≥ 5x − 3
For which of the following tables are all the values of x and their corresponding values of y solutions to the given inequality?
module1.rationale: At x = 4 the boundary is 17, and only one table keeps every value of y on the required side of the boundary at all three values of x.
reasons: put every value of y on the wrong side of the boundary line
the pair at x = 6 lies on the wrong side of the boundary line, although the other two are solutions
the pair at x = 4 lies on the wrong side of the boundary line, although the other two are solutions

module1.stem: An agronomist worked with 120 plots on a farm whose owner offered them for a study and randomly assigned them to two groups. One group was given a new fertilizer for 15 weeks and the other was given the usual one. The group given the new fertilizer had a significantly higher yield. Which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion from this study?
choices: There is an association between the new fertilizer and an increase in yield for the 120 plots in the study.
There is an association between the new fertilizer and an increase in yield for all the plots in the region.
The new fertilizer causes an increase in yield for the 120 plots in the study.
The new fertilizer causes an increase in yield for the plots on this farm.
latex: There is an association between the new fertilizer and an increase in yield for the 120 plots in the study.
There is an association between the new fertilizer and an increase in yield for all the plots in the region.
The new fertilizer causes an increase in yield for the 120 plots in the study.
The new fertilizer causes an increase in yield for the plots on this farm.
module1.rationale: The plots were randomly assigned, so the difference between the groups is a cause; they were not selected at random, so the conclusion reaches only the plots in the study.
reasons: settled for an association although the units were randomly assigned, which is what earns a cause
generalized from plots who were not selected at random, so the conclusion reaches only the plots in the study
generalized from plots who were not selected at random, so the conclusion reaches only the plots in the study

module1.stem:
³√(60z)(⁵√(60z))²
For what value of x is the given expression equivalent to (60z)^(12x), where z > 1?
module1.rationale: The two roots give exponents 1/3 and 2/5, which add to 11/15, and that has to equal 12x.

module1.stem: A number x is at most 14 more than 6 times the value of y. If the value of y is 6, what is the greatest possible value of x?
module1.rationale: The condition is x ≤ 6y + 14, and with y = 6 the right side is 50, so the greatest value x can take is 50.

module1.stem: What is the side length of a square that has the same area as a circle with a radius of 28?
module1.rationale: The circle has area pi(28)^2 = 784π; a square of that area has side 28√π.

module2_upper.figure: <svg viewBox="0 0 302 216" width="302" height="216" role="img" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><style>.ax{stroke:currentColor;stroke-width:1.4;fill:none}.gr{stroke:currentColor;stroke-width:.5;opacity:.28}.pt{fill:currentColor}.sg{stroke:currentColor;stroke-width:1.4;fill:none}.lb{fill:currentColor;font:11px ui-sans-serif,system-ui,sans-serif}.it{fill:currentColor;font:italic 13px ui-serif,Georgia,serif}</style><circle class="ax" cx="151" cy="108" r="76"/><line class="sg" x1="151" y1="108" x2="75.0" y2="108.0"/><line class="sg" x1="151" y1="108" x2="227.0" y2="108.0"/><line class="sg" x1="151" y1="108" x2="157.62" y2="32.29"/><line class="sg" x1="151" y1="108" x2="79.58" y2="82.01"/><circle class="pt" cx="151" cy="108" r="2.6"/><text class="it" x="145" y="123" text-anchor="end">O</text><circle class="pt" cx="75.0" cy="108.0" r="3.4"/><text class="it" x="66.0" y="112.0" text-anchor="end">D (−1, 0)</text><circle class="pt" cx="227.0" cy="108.0" r="3.4"/><text class="it" x="236.0" y="112.0" text-anchor="start">A (1, 0)</text><circle class="pt" cx="157.62" cy="32.29" r="3.4"/><text class="it" x="158.41" y="20.32" text-anchor="middle">B</text><circle class="pt" cx="79.58" cy="82.01" r="3.4"/><text class="it" x="71.13" y="82.93" text-anchor="end">C</text></svg>
module2_upper.rationale: A, O and D are collinear, so angle BOC is 180 − 85 − 20 = 75 degrees, which is 75 degrees.
reasons: subtracted only one of the two marked angles from 180 degrees
added the two marked angles instead of subtracting them from 180
subtracted the marked angles from a full turn instead of a straight angle

module2_upper.stem:
(a⁻⁶b³c³)(a³c⁶ + b⁹c⁻⁷)
Which of the following expressions is equivalent to the expression above?
module2_upper.rationale: a⁻⁶b³c³ multiplies each term inside the parentheses, and the exponents of each variable add.
reasons: multiplied only the first term inside the parentheses by the monomial
kept only the variables that both factors carry, dropping b from the first product and a from the second
left b out of both products because it is missing from one factor of each

module2_upper.stem: Which of the following is equivalent to (y + z/4)² ?
module2_upper.rationale: (y + z/4)² is y² plus twice y·z/4 plus (z/4)², and squaring a fraction squares its denominator too.
reasons: forgot to double the middle term and squared only the numerator of the fraction
left out the middle term and squared only the numerator of the fraction
left out the middle term of the square

module2_upper.stem:
y < −x + 2
Which point (x, y) is a solution to the given inequality in the xy-plane?
module2_upper.rationale: Substituting x = 3 and y = −3 gives −3 < −(3) + 2, or −3 < −1, which is true. Each of the other three points fails the inequality.
reasons: the point lies on the boundary line y = −x + 2, which a strict inequality leaves out
dropped a minus sign on a coefficient, which turns y < −x + 2 into y < x + 2
read the inequality the wrong way round, so the region on the other side of the boundary looked like the solution

module2_upper.stem:
(x + 1)(x + 3) = (x − 1)(x − 3) + 14
Which of the following is a solution to the given equation?
module2_upper.rationale: Both sides carry x², and what is left is 8x = 14, so x = 7/4.
reasons: solved for the wrong sign of x
cancelled both sides entirely and concluded that x is zero
forgot that the x terms appear twice over

module2_upper.stem: A number x is at most 5 less than 8 times the value of y. If the value of y is −11, what is the greatest possible value of x?
module2_upper.rationale: The condition is x ≤ 8y − 5, and with y = −11 the right side is −93, so the greatest value x can take is −93.

module2_upper.topic_name: One-Variable Data: Distributions and Measures of Centre and Spread
module2_upper.stem: The mean height of the 9 trees in an orchard is 8.5 feet. After the tallest tree is cut down, the mean height of the remaining 8 trees is 5.5 feet. What was the height, in feet, of the tree that was cut down?
module2_upper.rationale: The 9 values total 76.5 and the 8 that remain total 44, a difference of 32.5.
reasons: reported how far the mean fell, not the value that was taken away
swapped the two counts, using one fewer for the original group
subtracted 9 times the new mean instead of 8 times

module2_upper.stem:
4x + 9y = 30
36x + 81y = 270
For each real number r, which of the following points lies on the graph of each equation in the xy-plane for the given system?
module2_upper.rationale: The second equation is the first multiplied by 9, so the two draw the same line and any point on it will do. Letting y be r and solving 4x + 9y = 30 for x gives every such point at once.
reasons: divided r by the multiplier between the two equations and used the two right-hand sides as the shifts
solved for y but kept the sign of the x term, which changes the line
solved the equation for x but wrote that expression as the y-coordinate

module2_upper.stem: A botanist selected 150 seedlings at random from the seedlings in a greenhouse and randomly assigned them to two groups. One group was grown under a blue lamp for 4 weeks and the other under the usual lamp. The group grown under the blue lamp put on significantly more stem growth. Which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion from this study?
choices: There is an association between the blue lamp and an increase in stem growth for all seedlings of this species.
There is an association between the blue lamp and an increase in stem growth for the 150 seedlings in the study.
There is an association between the blue lamp and an increase in stem growth for the seedlings in this greenhouse.
The blue lamp causes an increase in stem growth for the seedlings in this greenhouse.
latex: There is an association between the blue lamp and an increase in stem growth for all seedlings of this species.
There is an association between the blue lamp and an increase in stem growth for the 150 seedlings in the study.
There is an association between the blue lamp and an increase in stem growth for the seedlings in this greenhouse.
The blue lamp causes an increase in stem growth for the seedlings in this greenhouse.
module2_upper.rationale: The seedlings were randomly assigned, so the difference between the groups is a cause; they were selected at random from the seedlings in this greenhouse, so the conclusion reaches that group.
reasons: generalized past the seedlings in this greenhouse, the group the seedlings were selected from
under-claimed twice over: random assignment earns a cause, and random selection earns the group the units came from
settled for an association although the units were randomly assigned, which is what earns a cause

In one week, Avery earned a total of s dollars for working at the two part-time jobs. The graph above represents all possible combinations of numbers of hours Avery could have worked at the two jobs to earn s dollars. What is the value of s ?

module2_upper.stem:
36, 37, 40, 41, x
The mean and the median of the five numbers above are equal. Which of the following is NOT a possible value of x ?
module2_upper.rationale: x can be 31, 38.5, and 46, depending on where it falls in the order; 25 is not one of them.
reasons: a value that does make the mean and the median equal, with x as the least of the five, leaving the middle value where it is
a value that does make the mean and the median equal, with x as the middle value of the five itself
a value that does make the mean and the median equal, with x as the greatest of the five, leaving the middle value where it is

module2_upper.stem: A shipping service restricts the dimensions of the boxes it will ship for a certain type of service. The restriction states that for boxes shaped like rectangular prisms, the sum of the perimeter of the base of the box and the height of the box cannot exceed 170 inches. The perimeter of the base is determined using the width and length of the box. If a box has a height of 70 inches and its length is 4 times the width, which inequality shows the allowable width x, in inches, of the box?
module2_upper.rationale: The base has perimeter 2(x + 4x) = 10x, so 10x + 70 ≤ 170, leaving x ≤ 10; a width is positive, so 0 < x ≤ 10.
reasons: added the width and the length once each instead of finding the whole perimeter
doubled the length but counted the width only once
used four widths, as though the base were a square

module2_upper.stem: Point O is the center of the circle above, and the measure of angle OMN is 45°. If the length of OC is 30, what is the measure, in degrees, of angle MON?

subtracted the base angle from 180 only once
near-miss arithmetic slip

module2_upper.stem: If √(z⁵)/⁶√(z²) = z^(a/b) for all positive values of z, what is the value of a/b ?
module2_upper.rationale: The two radicals are z^(5/2) and z^(1/3), and dividing subtracts the exponents.

module2_upper.stem: The expression (5n − 23)(19n + 6) is equivalent to the expression an² + bn + c, where a, b, and c are constants. What is the value of b?
module2_upper.rationale: The middle coefficient is the sum of the two cross products, 5 × 6 and −23 × 19.

module2_upper.stem:
−4x² − 18x + c = 0
In the given equation, c is a constant. The equation has exactly one solution. What is the value of c?
module2_upper.rationale: One solution means the discriminant is zero, so 324 + 16c = 0 and c = −20.25.

module1.stem:
|x − 9| = 15
What is one possible solution to the given equation?
module1.rationale: The quantity inside the bars is 15 or −15, so x = 24 or x = −6.

module1.stem: For a 2-week period in a town in Vermont, the lowest recorded temperature was 63 degrees Fahrenheit (°F) and the highest recorded temperature was 94°F. Which inequality is true for any recorded temperature t, in °F, in this town for this 2-week period?
module1.rationale: Every recorded value is at least the smallest, 63, and at most the largest, 94; both were recorded, so both ends belong to the range and 63 ≤ t ≤ 94.
reasons: kept only the smallest recorded value and read it as a cap rather than as the bottom of the range
used the largest recorded value as the bottom of the range and the sum of the two as the top
kept only the largest recorded value and read it as a floor rather than as the top of the range

module1.stem: Which expression is equivalent to 5y¹⁰z³ + 25y²z³ ?
module1.rationale: 5y²z³ divides both terms, and dividing y¹⁰ by y² subtracts the exponents.
reasons: divided the exponents and dropped the second term
divided the exponents instead of subtracting them
multiplied the two terms left inside instead of adding them

module1.stem:
20x − 2y > 18
Which of the following inequalities is equivalent to the inequality above?
module1.rationale: Every term of 20x − 2y > 18 is a multiple of 2, and dividing a strict inequality by a positive number leaves it pointing the same way, so it is 10x − y > 9.
reasons: wrote the two terms the other way round and divided the constant by the first coefficient
divided each term by its own coefficient instead of by the factor all three share
divided correctly but then exchanged the two coefficients

module1.stem: On a car trip, Ines and Peter each drove for part of the trip, and the total distance they drove was at least 300 miles. Ines drove at an average speed of 70 miles per hour (mph), and Peter drove at an average speed of 25 mph. Which of the following inequalities represents this situation, where x is the number of hours Ines drove and y is the number of hours Peter drove?
module1.rationale: Ines covers 70 miles in each of the x hours, which is 70x, and Peter covers 25 miles in each of the y hours, which is 25y; the distance altogether is at least 300, so 70x + 25y ≥ 300.
reasons: gave each driver the other driver's average speed and read the limit as a maximum instead of a minimum
read the limit as a maximum instead of a minimum
gave each driver the other driver's average speed

module1.stem: A certain elephant weighs 270 pounds at birth and gains more than 5 but less than 9 pounds per day during its first year. Which of the following inequalities represents all possible weights w, in pounds, for the elephant 105 days after birth?
module1.rationale: The smallest the quantity can be is 270 + 105(5) = 795, and the largest is 270 + 105(9) = 1,215; the multiplier is positive, so the ends keep their order and 795 < w < 1,215.
reasons: multiplied the birth weight by each end of the range instead of adding the amount the rate builds up
added the birth weight at the top of the range but not at the bottom
left the birth weight out of both ends of the range

module1.stem: In the circle shown with center O, arc JDV has a central angle of x = 10 degrees and a length of 6π meters. What is the length, in meters, of arc JKV?

module1.topic_name: One-Variable Data: Distributions and Measures of Centre and Spread
module1.stem:
13, 5, 14, 10, 1
The mean of the list of numbers above is what fraction of the sum of the five numbers?
module1.rationale: The mean is the sum divided by 5, so it is one fifth of the sum whatever the numbers are.

module1.stem:
(n + 1/2)((1/2)n + 5/2)
The expression above is equivalent to an² + bn + c, where a, b, and c are constants. What is the value of b?
module1.rationale: The middle coefficient is the sum of the two cross products, 1 × 5/2 and 1/2 × 1/2.

module1.stem:
4x − 2y > −5
Which point (x, y) is a solution to the given inequality in the xy-plane?
module1.rationale: Substituting x = 2 and y = −3 gives 4(2) − 2(−3) > −5, or 14 > −5, which is true. Each of the other three points fails the inequality.
reasons: substituted the coordinates in the other order, putting the y-value in for x
read the inequality the wrong way round, so the region on the other side of the boundary looked like the solution
dropped a minus sign on a coefficient, which turns 4x − 2y > −5 into 4x + 2y > −5

module1.stem: A model estimates that whales from the genus Eschrichtius travel 119 to 122 miles in the ocean each day during their migration. Based on this model, which inequality represents the estimated total number of miles, x, one of these whales could travel in 39 days of its migration?
module1.rationale: Each of the 39 days adds between 119 and 122 miles, so the smallest total is (119)(39) and the largest is (122)(39); multiplying by a positive number keeps the two ends in order, so (119)(39) ≤ x ≤ (122)(39).
reasons: added the two quantities instead of multiplying them
divided by the quantity that should have been multiplied, which also turns the two ends round
subtracted the two quantities instead of multiplying them

module1.stem:
(a² − 8a + 4) + (2a² + 5a − 8)
Which of the following is equivalent to the expression above?
module1.rationale: Like terms are collected power by power.
reasons: subtracted the constant terms instead of adding them
multiplied the coefficients of the like terms instead of adding them
lined the terms up as written and added the exponents too

module1.stem: A cargo helicopter delivers only 30-pound packages and 190-pound packages. For each delivery trip, the cargo helicopter must carry at least 12 packages, and the total weight of the packages can be at most 1,800 pounds. What is the maximum number of 190-pound packages that the cargo helicopter can carry per trip?
module1.rationale: Carrying 12 of the lighter packages weighs 360 pounds, and each swap to a heavier one adds 160 pounds. The cap leaves 1,440 pounds to spend on swaps, so at most 9 of the packages can be the heavier kind.
reasons: divided the weight left over by the heavier package rather than by the difference between the two
stopped one swap short of the weight the load allows
rounded the number of swaps up instead of down

module1.stem: A researcher selected 60 members at random from the members of a health center and randomly assigned them to two groups. One group used a sleep app for 7 weeks and the other did not. The group that used the app slept significantly longer each night. Which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion from this study?
choices: The sleep app causes an increase in nightly sleep for the 60 members in the study.
The sleep app causes an increase in nightly sleep for the members of the health center.
The sleep app causes an increase in nightly sleep for all adults in the city.
There is an association between the sleep app and an increase in nightly sleep for the members of the health center.
latex: The sleep app causes an increase in nightly sleep for the 60 members in the study.
The sleep app causes an increase in nightly sleep for the members of the health center.
The sleep app causes an increase in nightly sleep for all adults in the city.
There is an association between the sleep app and an increase in nightly sleep for the members of the health center.
module1.rationale: The members were randomly assigned, so the difference between the groups is a cause; they were selected at random from the members of the health center, so the conclusion reaches that group.
reasons: kept the conclusion inside the study although the units were selected at random from a whole group
generalized past the members of the health center, the group the members were selected from
settled for an association although the units were randomly assigned, which is what earns a cause

module1.stem: If √(z⁷)/⁵√(z²) = z^(a/b) for all positive values of z, what is the value of a/b ?
module1.rationale: The two radicals are z^(7/2) and z^(2/5), and dividing subtracts the exponents.

module1.stem: A number x is at least 7 more than 2 times the value of y. If the value of y is −7, what is the least possible value of x?
module1.rationale: The condition is x ≥ 2y + 7, and with y = −7 the right side is −7, so the least value x can take is −7.

module1.stem: The mean height of the 8 trees in an orchard is 29 feet. After the tallest tree is cut down, the mean height of the remaining 7 trees is 28 feet. What was the height, in feet, of the tree that was cut down?
module1.rationale: The 8 values total 232 and the 7 that remain total 196, a difference of 36.
reasons: reported how far the mean fell, not the value that was taken away
subtracted 8 times the new mean instead of 7 times
added the two means

module1.stem:
8x + 7y = 7
48x + 42y = 42
For each real number r, which of the following points lies on the graph of each equation in the xy-plane for the given system?
module1.rationale: The second equation is the first multiplied by 6, so the two draw the same line and any point on it will do. Letting y be r and solving 8x + 7y = 7 for x gives every such point at once.
reasons: solved the equation for x but wrote that expression as the y-coordinate
solved for y but kept the sign of the x term, which changes the line
divided r by the multiplier between the two equations and used the two right-hand sides as the shifts

module1.stem:
x² + 18x + c = 0
In the given equation, c is a constant. The equation has exactly one solution. What is the value of c?
module1.rationale: One solution means the discriminant is zero, so 324 − 4c = 0 and c = 81.

module2_lower.stem: During spring migration, a dragonfly traveled a minimum of 60 miles and a maximum of 103 miles between stopover locations. Which inequality represents this situation, where d is a possible distance, in miles, this dragonfly traveled between stopover locations during spring migration?
module2_lower.rationale: Every recorded value is at least the smallest, 60, and at most the largest, 103; both were recorded, so both ends belong to the range and 60 ≤ d ≤ 103.
reasons: used the largest recorded value as the bottom of the range and the sum of the two as the top
kept only the smallest recorded value and read it as a cap rather than as the bottom of the range
kept only the largest recorded value and read it as a floor rather than as the top of the range

module2_lower.stem: On a car trip, Jamal and Beatriz each drove for part of the trip, and the total distance they drove was at least 180 miles. Jamal drove at an average speed of 70 miles per hour (mph), and Beatriz drove at an average speed of 60 mph. Which of the following inequalities represents this situation, where x is the number of hours Jamal drove and y is the number of hours Beatriz drove?
module2_lower.rationale: Jamal covers 70 miles in each of the x hours, which is 70x, and Beatriz covers 60 miles in each of the y hours, which is 60y; the distance altogether is at least 180, so 70x + 60y ≥ 180.
reasons: read the limit as a maximum instead of a minimum
gave each driver the other driver's average speed and read the limit as a maximum instead of a minimum
gave each driver the other driver's average speed

71, 76, 65, 66, 90

reported the least value instead of the difference

module2_lower.stem: Normal body temperature for an adult is between 96.3°F and 98°F, inclusive. If Ken, an adult, has a body temperature that is considered to be normal, which of the following could be that body temperature?
module2_lower.rationale: A normal body temperature is anywhere from 96.3°F to 98°F, and 96.7°F is the only one of the four printed values in that range.
reasons: below the lower end of the range, 96.3°F, by more than a degree
just below the lower end of the range, 96.3°F, which a normal reading has to reach
above the upper end of the range, 98°F, which a normal reading cannot pass

module2_lower.rationale: Each tile covers 7 square inches, so the 89 blue tiles cover 623 and the green tiles have to cover the remaining 609.

How many distinct real solutions are there to the given equation?
module2_lower.rationale: The equation has a discriminant of 0, so it has exactly one real solution.
reasons: took the square root of a negative number as though it were positive
read the sign of the discriminant the wrong way round, and concluded that the curve never meets the axis

module2_lower.stem: Which of the following is equivalent to n² + 16n + 7 ?
module2_lower.rationale: Half of 16 is 8, and (n + 8)² already carries 64, so −57 is what is left to reach 7.
reasons: halved the middle coefficient with the wrong sign and corrected the wrong way too
halved the middle coefficient but changed its sign
added the correction instead of subtracting it

module2_lower.stem: Which of the following is an equivalent form of t² − 3 ?
module2_lower.rationale: 3 is not a perfect square, but it is still √3 squared, so the expression is a difference of two squares.
reasons: looked for two whole numbers multiplying to −3 instead of taking a square root
used the same sign in both brackets, which gives a square rather than a difference of squares
used the same negative sign in both brackets

y ≥ −x + 4

module2_lower.rationale: At x = 3 the boundary is 1, and only one table keeps every value of y on the required side of the boundary at all three values of x.

Which of the following is a solution to the given equation?
module2_lower.rationale: Both sides carry x², and what is left is 24x = −18, so x = −3/4.
reasons: forgot that the x terms appear twice over
cancelled both sides entirely and concluded that x is zero
solved for the wrong sign of x

module2_lower.stem: A circle has a diameter of 24. What is the side length of a square whose area is equal to the area of this circle?
module2_lower.rationale: The circle has area pi(12)^2 = 144π; a square of that area has side 12√π.
reasons: found the area as πr, forgetting to square the radius, and then took the square root
used the radius as the side length
used the diameter as the radius

module2_lower.stem: A number x is at most 10 more than 2 times the value of y. If the value of y is −9, what is the greatest possible value of x?
module2_lower.rationale: The condition is x ≤ 2y + 10, and with y = −9 the right side is −8, so the greatest value x can take is −8.

module2_lower.stem: A shipping service restricts the dimensions of the boxes it will ship for a certain type of service. The restriction states that for boxes shaped like rectangular prisms, the sum of the perimeter of the base of the box and the height of the box cannot exceed 170 inches. The perimeter of the base is determined using the width and length of the box. If a box has a height of 70 inches and its length is 3 times the width, which inequality shows the allowable width x, in inches, of the box?
module2_lower.rationale: The base has perimeter 2(x + 3x) = 8x, so 8x + 70 ≤ 170, leaving x ≤ 12 1/2; a width is positive, so 0 < x ≤ 12 1/2.
reasons: doubled the length but counted the width only once
added the width and the length once each instead of finding the whole perimeter
left the height out of the cap altogether

reasons: read the limit as a maximum instead of a minimum
attached each price to the other kind of item

module2_upper.rationale: The middle coefficient is the sum of the two cross products, 2 × 3/2 and 3/2 × 2/3.

module2_upper.stem: Points M, N, and T lie on the circle shown. On this circle, minor arc MN has a length of 51 inches and major arc MTN has a length of 102 inches. What is the circumference, in inches, of the circle shown?

module2_upper.rationale: The two arcs make up the whole circle, so the circumference is 51 + 102 = 153.
reasons: gave the minor arc instead of the whole circumference
gave the major arc instead of the whole circumference
doubled the major arc

module2_upper.stem: Which expression is equivalent to x² − 6?
module2_upper.rationale: 6 is not a perfect square, but it is still √6 squared, so the expression is a difference of two squares.
reasons: used the same negative sign in both brackets
looked for two whole numbers multiplying to −6 instead of taking a square root
used the same sign in both brackets, which gives a square rather than a difference of squares

module2_upper.stem: In the xy-plane above, points P, Q, R, and T lie on the circle with center O. The degree measures of angles POQ and ROT are 80° and 65°, respectively. What is the radian measure of angle QOR ?

module2_upper.stem: Which of the following is equivalent to (6yz)(y)(2z)?
module2_upper.rationale: The coefficients multiply and the exponents of y and of z each add, giving 12y²z².
reasons: added the three coefficients instead of multiplying them
added the exponents of y but left z alone
multiplied the coefficients but added none of the exponents

module2_upper.stem:
(2n − 2.4)² − (5.2n² − 6)
Which of the following expressions is equivalent to the expression above?
module2_upper.rationale: (2n − 2.4)² is 4n² − 9.6n + 5.76, and every term of the second bracket is then subtracted.
reasons: doubled each term instead of squaring the binomial, so the middle term never appeared
doubled each term instead of squaring and then added the two constants rather than subtracting
subtracted the two constant terms the wrong way round

module2_upper.stem: A cargo helicopter delivers only 30-pound packages and 220-pound packages. For each delivery trip, the cargo helicopter must carry at least 9 packages, and the total weight of the packages can be at most 650 pounds. What is the maximum number of 220-pound packages that the cargo helicopter can carry per trip?
module2_upper.rationale: Carrying 9 of the lighter packages weighs 270 pounds, and each swap to a heavier one adds 190 pounds. The cap leaves 380 pounds to spend on swaps, so at most 2 of the packages can be the heavier kind.
reasons: stopped one swap short of the weight the load allows
rounded the number of swaps up instead of down
near-miss arithmetic slip

module2_upper.stem: Which of the following expressions is equivalent to k² + 12k − 20 ?
module2_upper.rationale: Half of 12 is 6, and (k + 6)² already carries 36, so −56 is what is left to reach −20.
reasons: added the correction instead of subtracting it
halved the middle coefficient but changed its sign
halved the middle coefficient with the wrong sign and corrected the wrong way too

module2_upper.stem: A number x is at least 7 more than 3 times the value of y. If the value of y is −11, what is the least possible value of x?
module2_upper.rationale: The condition is x ≥ 3y + 7, and with y = −11 the right side is −26, so the least value x can take is −26.

module2_upper.stem: A botanist selected 75 seedlings at random from the seedlings in a greenhouse and recorded which of them a grower had already placed under a blue lamp. Over 6 weeks, the seedlings under the blue lamp put on significantly more stem growth. Which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion from this study?
choices: There is an association between the blue lamp and an increase in stem growth for the 75 seedlings in the study.
The blue lamp causes an increase in stem growth for the seedlings in this greenhouse.
There is an association between the blue lamp and an increase in stem growth for the seedlings in this greenhouse.
There is an association between the blue lamp and an increase in stem growth for all seedlings of this species.
latex: There is an association between the blue lamp and an increase in stem growth for the 75 seedlings in the study.
The blue lamp causes an increase in stem growth for the seedlings in this greenhouse.
There is an association between the blue lamp and an increase in stem growth for the seedlings in this greenhouse.
There is an association between the blue lamp and an increase in stem growth for all seedlings of this species.
module2_upper.rationale: The seedlings were not randomly assigned, so the difference between the groups is an association and not a cause; they were selected at random from the seedlings in this greenhouse, so the conclusion reaches that group.
reasons: kept the conclusion inside the study although the units were selected at random from a whole group
read random selection as random assignment: selecting units at random earns a population, not a cause
generalized past the seedlings in this greenhouse, the group the seedlings were selected from

module2_upper.stem:
3x + 7y = 26
27x + 63y = 234
For each real number r, which of the following points lies on the graph of each equation in the xy-plane for the given system?
module2_upper.rationale: The second equation is the first multiplied by 9, so the two draw the same line and any point on it will do. Letting y be r and solving 3x + 7y = 26 for x gives every such point at once.
reasons: solved the equation for x but wrote that expression as the y-coordinate
solved for y but kept the sign of the x term, which changes the line
divided r by the multiplier between the two equations and used the two right-hand sides as the shifts

module2_upper.stem: Data set A consists of the ages of 13 members and data set B consists of the ages of 13 other members. The table shows the frequency distribution of the ages. Which of the following statements best compares the means of the two data sets?
choices: The mean of data set A is equal to the mean of data set B.
There is not enough information to compare the means of the data sets.
The mean of data set A is greater than the mean of data set B.
The mean of data set A is less than the mean of data set B.
latex: The mean of data set A is equal to the mean of data set B.
There is not enough information to compare the means of the data sets.
The mean of data set A is greater than the mean of data set B.
The mean of data set A is less than the mean of data set B.
module2_upper.rationale: Data set A has mean 344/13 and data set B has mean 358/13.
reasons: saw the same values and the same set of frequencies in both columns and concluded the means must match
assumed a frequency table does not pin down a mean
weighted the values the wrong way round: the frequencies say how many of each value there are, not how large they are

module2_upper.stem:
Data set A consists of 11 positive integers less than 48. The list shown gives 10 of the integers from data set A.
35, 34, 31, 32, 32, 40, 34, 34, 40, 48
The mean of these 10 integers is 36. If the mean of data set A is an integer that is greater than 36, what is the value of the largest integer from data set A?
module2_upper.rationale: The 10 listed integers total 360. Only 47 makes 360 + x divide by 11 to give a whole number above 36.

module2_upper.stem: A shipping service restricts the dimensions of the boxes it will ship for a certain type of service. The restriction states that for boxes shaped like rectangular prisms, the sum of the perimeter of the base of the box and the height of the box cannot exceed 200 inches. The perimeter of the base is determined using the width and length of the box. If a box has a height of 90 inches and its length is 3 times the width, which inequality shows the allowable width x, in inches, of the box?
module2_upper.rationale: The base has perimeter 2(x + 3x) = 8x, so 8x + 90 ≤ 200, leaving x ≤ 13 3/4; a width is positive, so 0 < x ≤ 13 3/4.
reasons: left the height out of the cap altogether
doubled the length but counted the width only once
added the width and the length once each instead of finding the whole perimeter

module2_upper.stem: What is the side length of a square that has the same area as a circle with a circumference of 20π?
module2_upper.rationale: The circle has area pi(10)^2 = 100π; a square of that area has side 10√π.
reasons: found the area as πr, forgetting to square the radius, and then took the square root
used the radius as the side length
used πr, forgetting to square the radius or take the root

module2_upper.stem:
⁷√(60n)(⁵√(60n))²
For what value of x is the given expression equivalent to (60n)^(12x), where n > 1?
module2_upper.rationale: The two roots give exponents 1/7 and 2/5, which add to 19/35, and that has to equal 12x.

module2_upper.stem:
−16x² − 12x + c = 0
In the given equation, c is a constant. The equation has exactly one solution. What is the value of c?
module2_upper.rationale: One solution means the discriminant is zero, so 144 + 64c = 0 and c = −2.25.

module2_upper.stem: Which of the following is equivalent to (j² + 4j + 4)/(j + 6) ?
module2_upper.rationale: j² + 4j + 4 is (j + 6)(j − 2) + 16, and only 16 is left over.
reasons: used the divisor's constant with the wrong sign when finding the quotient
used the divisor's constant with the wrong sign, and then added the quotient's constant to the remainder instead of multiplying it by the divisor's root
subtracted the divisor's constant from the remainder instead of multiplying by it
